colt-m1911: A semi-automatic pistol seen from the side, with slide, trigger guard, and a grip marked by two round rivets, plus a small ejected casing above.
column-vase: A handled urn topped by a flat lid, resting on an Ionic column capital with two scrolled volutes.
coma: An oval head with shut curved eyes and a downturned mouth, its forehead bearing a pale disc crossed by a heartbeat trace line.
comb: A hair comb tilted diagonally, with a curved solid spine above a row of long parallel teeth.
combination-lock: A padlock with a tall arched shackle and a square body bearing three numbered dials reading 8, 3 and 6.
comet-spark: A blazing comet head with a curling spiral core and several tapering flame-like tails streaming off to one side.
commercial-airplane: An airliner seen from above, flying diagonally with swept wings, tail fins, and cockpit windows marked near the nose.
compact-disc: A disc with a small central hole ringed by a band, its face split by narrow radial wedges cut from the rim toward the center.
companion-cube: A square cube face with corner panels and a central circle bearing a heart, the Weighted Companion Cube from Portal.
compass: A compass rose: a long double-pointed needle crossing a ring bordered by radiating tick marks, the standard emblem of navigation and direction-finding.
computer-fan: A circular cooling fan with curved blades around a central hub, ringed by a round frame with a mounting dot at each corner.
computing: Three rows of binary digits, reading 0100, 0011 and 1001, the conventional shorthand for computer code and digital data.
concentration-orb: A solid sphere encircled by two tapering crescent arcs that spiral around it, a common shorthand for swirling energy or an arcane orb.
concentric-crescents: A set of nested crescent rings spiralling inward within a circular disc, forming a swirling target-like vortex.
concrete-bag: A large sack with a gathered top standing beside a pointed mason's trowel and a stepped course of laid bricks.
condor-emblem: A heraldic bird of prey with raised wings and fanned tail, seen head-on against an arc and radiating rays.
condylura-skull: A broad angular animal skull with two large triangular eye sockets, its snout splitting into a downward fan of tapering rays like a star-nosed mole's tentacled nose.
confirmed: A checkmark within a thick circular ring, the standard sign for approval, completion, or confirmation.
confrontation: Two angry faces in profile pressed nose to nose with furrowed brows and shouting mouths, radiating lines bursting upward between them.
congress: A domed capitol building with a flagpole atop the dome, tiers of columns and a broad base, an emblem of government and legislature.
conqueror: A figure standing atop a hill with one foot raised on a rock, holding a tall banner pole with a small pennant, a classic image of conquest.
console-controller: A video game gamepad with a cross-shaped directional pad, two round analog sticks, and four round face buttons.
contortionist: A human figure bent backward into an extreme arch, standing on one leg with the torso curved over and the other leg and arms extended overhead.
contract: Four solid triangular arrows set at the corners of a square, all pointing diagonally inward toward the center, the standard sign for shrinking or collapsing a view.
control-tower: An airport control tower with a flared observation deck and antenna mast, beside a low terminal building with windows and a door, with an airplane above.
convergence-target: Four chevrons arranged around an empty center, each pointing inward toward the middle, a common targeting or converge marker.
conversation: Two overlapping oval speech balloons with tails, each filled with bars of blocky text standing in for lines of dialogue.
converse-shoe: A high-top canvas sneaker in side profile, with a round ankle patch, lacing slits, rubber toe cap and thick flat sole.
convict: A bust of a person in a flat-topped cap wearing a horizontally striped shirt, the conventional depiction of a prisoner.
convince: Two faces in profile close together, one leaning in to speak or whisper toward the other's ear.
conway-life-glider: A three-by-three grid with filled circles in the top-middle, middle-right, and all three bottom cells, the glider pattern from Conway's Game of Life.
cook: A bust of a chef wearing a tall toque and a double-breasted jacket with two buttons.
cookie: A slightly irregular round cookie dotted with scattered oval chips.
cooking-glove: An oven mitt with a rounded body, a thumb jutting to the side, and a hanging loop at the cuff.
cooking-pot: A deep cooking pot with side handles and a domed lid topped by a knob.
cool-spices: A conical mound of powder surrounded by scattered grains, with diamonds and four-pointed sparkles rising above it, the usual shorthand for magic or enchantment.
cooler: A cooler chest with a lid and handle, marked with a snowflake on its front face.
cootie-catcher: A folded paper fortune teller seen from above, its four pointed flaps rising in sharp triangular peaks around a central crease.
coral: A branching coral formation rising from a short stem, its limbs forking repeatedly into slender tapering tips.
cork-hat: A wide-brimmed bush hat with strings hanging from the brim, each ending in a dangling cork.
corked-tube: A tilted test tube with a rounded bottom, partly filled with dark liquid and topped by a stopper.
corkscrew: A corkscrew with a thick hourglass-shaped handle set diagonally above a helical spiral worm.
corn: An ear of corn angled upward, its kernels shown as a diamond grid, with husk leaves peeled back on either side.
corner-explosion: A jagged starburst of sharp spikes bursting outward from the lower-right corner, the standard depiction of a blast or explosion.
corner-flag: A flag on a tall pole planted where two lines meet in a curved corner arc, with a soccer ball resting beside it.
cornucopia: A curved, tapering horn with spiraling bands spilling out a grape cluster, an apple, a pear and a wheat stalk, the classic horn of plenty signifying abundance and harvest.
coronation: A standing figure holding a pointed crown above a kneeling figure who bows before them, the classic image of a coronation or knighting.
corporal: Two stacked upward-pointing chevrons with slightly curved arms, a military rank insignia.
corset: A bustier-style corset with cupped bust panels, a criss-cross laced front seam, and boning lines flaring at the hips.
corsica: The silhouette of the island of Corsica, with its jagged western coastline and the small Cap Corse peninsula at the top.
cosmic-egg: A solid egg marked with a circle enclosing a four-pointed star, a linked constellation of dots, and sparkles scattered around it, suggesting cosmic creation.
cotton-flower: A cotton boll of several rounded fluffy lobes atop a slender curving stem with a pair of narrow leaves.
covered-jar: A wide-bellied ceramic jar topped by a domed lid with a small knob finial, of the kind used as an urn or ginger jar.
cow: A cow standing in profile with horns, tail curling up, and pale patches on its flank and legs.
cowboy-boot: A tall cowboy boot in profile with a stacked heel and a spiked rowel spur mounted at the back.
cowboy-holster: A leather revolver holster hanging from a belt with cartridge loops, the gun's grip protruding at the top, standard gear of the Old West gunslinger.
cowled: A hooded head seen from the front, the shadowed face showing only two narrow slanted eyes, an emblem of rogues, cultists and assassins.
cpu: An octagonal microchip with a rectangular core panel and short pin bars projecting from all four sides.
cpu-shot: A tilted microchip with pin rows along its edges, marked by a jagged burst and a hole blasted through its center.
crab: A crab seen from above, its broad domed shell with two round eyes and a large pincer claw to either side.
crab-claw: A crab or crustacean pincer claw seen from the side, its upper part edged with several sharp spikes and the lower jaw curving to a hooked point.
cracked-alien-skull: An alien skull with a broad domed cranium split by jagged cracks, tapering to a narrow fanged jaw with pointed teeth.
cracked-ball-dunk: A ball splitting into cracked segments amid a spiked burst, with a curving arc sweeping over it to trace the ball's descending trajectory.
cracked-disc: A solid circular disc split by a wide jagged lightning-shaped crack running from top to bottom, separating it into two broken halves.
cracked-glass: A square pane shattered into angular shards, with jagged fracture lines radiating outward from a central impact point.
cracked-helm: A knight's great helm with a T-shaped eye and nose slit, split by a jagged crack across its crown.
cracked-mask: A rounded face mask with curved eye slits, a broad grinning mouth slit, and a jagged crack splitting its brow.
cracked-saber: A curved saber blade broken into several separated fragments along jagged cracks, the tip splintering away from the body of the blade.
cracked-shield: A pointed heraldic shield split down the middle by a jagged lightning-bolt-shaped crack, a common sign of broken defenses.
crafting: A rectangular block and a circle on the left, joined by converging arrows pointing right toward a cylinder, indicating components combined into a finished product.
crags: A circular medallion filled with steep angular rock pillars and cliff faces separated by narrow gaps, depicting a craggy stone outcrop.
crane: A tower crane with a peaked cable stay above a horizontal jib, a vertical mast on splayed legs, and a hook line lowering a hanging load.
credits-currency: A bold letter G crossed by a vertical bar extending above and below it, in the manner of a currency sign.
crenel-crown: A jagged crown with a tall central spike flanked by shorter angular points, set with a pointed gem at its center.
crenulated-shield: A heater shield topped with square battlement crenellations, its face divided into alternating light and dark quarters like a heraldic quartering.
crescent-blade: A broad crescent-shaped blade mounted at the end of a long tapering haft that runs diagonally to the upper corner.
crescent-staff: A staff with a banded, tapered shaft topped by a hooked crescent moon cradling a solid orb, with radiating light shards beside the crescent's tip.
crested-helmet: A Corinthian-style helmet seen from the front, with tapering upright crest, eye slits and a narrow nose guard, an emblem of Spartan warriors.
cricket: A cricket or grasshopper seen in profile, with long trailing antennae, bulging eye, folded wing and bent jumping hind leg.
cricket-bat: A cricket bat angled diagonally with its long tapered handle, beside a small ball marked with a curved seam line.
crime-scene-tape: A doorway crossed by crisscrossing strips of tape, with a small keyhole-like circle at the center, the standard barrier sealing off a crime scene.
croc-jaws: A crocodile's gaping jaws seen in profile, upper and lower snouts lined with interlocking triangular teeth and a small eye near the top.
croc-sword: A diagonally angled sword with a straight crossguard, flared pommel, and a broad blade whose lower edge is cut into jagged saw-like teeth.
croissant: A crescent-shaped croissant with a broad central lobe flanked by tapering curved tips, divided by narrow segment lines.
croissants-pupil: An eye-like spiral of nested crescent shapes curling around a central disc split by a slit pupil, resembling a reptilian or cat's eye.
crook-flail: A shepherd's crook and a three-stranded flail crossed over one another, both rendered in segmented beaded blocks, the paired regalia of Egyptian pharaohs and Osiris denoting kingship.
cross-flare: A thick ring crossed by a four-armed X-shaped burst, with one arm extending far beyond the ring in a long tapering spike.
cross-mark: A ragged X formed by two crossing sweeps of splintered, tapering slashes, the standard mark for cancellation or a wrong answer.
cross-shield: A heater shield with a peaked top, studded with rivets along its border and bearing a tapered cross with flared arms, an emblem of crusader knights and holy protection.
crossbow: A crossbow seen at an angle, with curved bow limbs, taut string and a stock crossing behind it, a loaded bolt aimed toward the upper right.
crosscut-saw: A two-man crosscut saw blade set diagonally, its lower edge lined with large triangular teeth and a straight handle bar at each end.
crossed-air-flows: Two sets of long tapering curved streaks sweeping in from different directions and crossing near the center, a common shorthand for gusting wind or air currents.
crossed-axes: Two broad-bladed battle axes crossed at their curving hafts, blades flaring outward at the top.
crossed-bones: Two long bones with knobbed ends crossed in an X, the familiar death or poison marker paired with skulls on pirate flags.
crossed-chains: Two heavy chains of elongated links crossing each other diagonally in an X, a common emblem of bondage or restraint.
crossed-claws: A massive crustacean pincer whose two jaws meet in jagged interlocking teeth, with a smaller barbed claw tip beside it.
crossed-pistols: Two flintlock-style pistols with long barrels and curved grips crossed in an X, a common emblem of duelling, piracy, or marksmanship.
crossed-sabres: Two curved sabres with knuckle-guard hilts crossed in an X, an emblem of swordsmanship, piracy and military honor.
crossed-slashes: Two tapering crescent slash marks crossing each other, the sweeping curved strokes used to show a blade's cutting arc.
crossed-swords: Two broad-bladed swords crossed in an X with their fullers and crossguards visible, the common emblem of battle or melee combat.
crosshair: A circle crossed by four short tick marks at top, bottom, left and right with a small plus sign at its center, the standard reticle for aiming.
crosshair-arrow: An arrow with barbed fletching and a broad head striking diagonally through a circular crosshair reticle with crossing sight lines, indicating an accurate hit on target.
crossroad: A road seen in perspective splitting into two branches, with a dashed center line and two arrow shapes pointing left and right above the fork.
crow-dive: A crow plunging in a steep dive, wings swept back with splayed feather tips and tail fanned, beak open and talons tucked.
crow-nest: A ship's crow's nest basket atop a mast, holding a lookout figure raising a spyglass, with a pennant flag flying from the mast.
crowbar: A crowbar with a long straight shaft angling up to a curved, forked claw end.
crown: A pointed crown with sharp spikes, ringed with circular gems on its band and floating diamond and dot shapes above, an emblem of royalty.
crown-coin: A thick coin seen at an angle, its face bearing a three-pointed crown ringed by a border of dashes, with a milled edge along the rim.
crown-of-thorns: A twisted circular wreath of thorny branches bristling with sharp spikes, the crown of thorns associated with the Passion of Christ.
crowned-explosion: A solid disc ringed by a burst of jagged spikes and shards radiating outward, the conventional sign for an explosion or blast.
crowned-heart: A heart marked with a crescent highlight, with a three-pointed crown bearing round and diamond gems floating above it.
crowned-skull: A skull with slanted eye sockets, a diamond-shaped nose hole and bared teeth, topped by a spiked crown, a common emblem of a death-king or lich.
crucifix: A tilted wooden cross with squared beams shown in three-quarter perspective, a Christian emblem often used to ward off vampires and undead.
cruiser: A warship seen head-on with a boxy superstructure and mast, riding above wavy horizontal water lines.
crumbling-ball: A sphere breaking apart, with angular shards flaking off its upper-left side and drifting away as scattered fragments.
crush: A heavy rectangular block with a jagged, toothed lower edge poised above a small circle, depicting something about to be crushed.
cryo-chamber: A human figure standing inside an upright rectangular tank with bubbles rising beside it, a hooded top fixture, and curved arcs and dashes flanking and beneath it.
crypt-entrance: A stone archway on two square columns with a keystone, strung with a tattered spiderweb across the arch, marking a long-abandoned tomb doorway.
crystal-ball: A sphere marked with two dark oval highlights, resting on a tiered flared base, the classic scrying orb of fortune-tellers.
crystal-bars: A cluster of five elongated faceted crystal shards of varying sizes, with pointed tips and internal edge lines.
crystal-cluster: A burst of sharp faceted crystal shards radiating outward from a common center, with a slim star-shaped gap left at the middle.
crystal-earrings: A pair of matching earrings, each with a curved hook above a bar and a long faceted kite-shaped gem tapering to a point.
crystal-eye: An almond-shaped eye whose round iris is faceted into gem-like panels, suggesting a crystal or jewel set in place of the pupil.
crystal-growth: A cluster of tall pointed crystal shards of varying heights rising from a common base.
crystal-shine: A faceted hexagonal gem split into wedge-shaped facets, framed by two curved arcs and a ring of radiating spikes and droplets suggesting brilliant light.
crystal-shrine: A cluster of angular crystal shards rising from a stepped pedestal, ringed by four-pointed sparkles that conventionally indicate magic or enchantment.
crystal-wand: A diagonal wand with a banded shaft, topped by an angular faceted crystal held in a claw-like setting of prongs.
crystalize: A teardrop shape whose interior is divided into faceted crystal panels by radiating lines, with rounded solid wedges filling the segments.
cuauhtli: An eagle's head in profile with a hooked beak, round eye, and layered plumes sweeping back, styled after Aztec glyph carving.
cube: A cube seen in isometric view, its top and two side faces separated by thin gaps.
cubeforce: Three isometric cubes stacked in a pyramid, each face marked with a curved wedge shape.
cubes: Three cubes of differing sizes with slightly bulging faces, each shown in three-quarter view with its top and two side faces separated by thin gaps.
cuckoo-clock: A gabled house-shaped cuckoo clock with a clock face and two hanging pinecone weights, flanked by two musical notes.
cultist: A hooded figure fully draped in a pointed, drooping-tipped robe with two pale eye holes and a ragged fringed hem, an emblem of secret cults.
cupcake: A cupcake in a fluted paper wrapper topped with a tall swirl of piped frosting.
cupidon-arrow: A heart pierced diagonally by an arrow whose barbed head and shaft emerge below and whose tail juts above, Cupid's emblem of love infatuation.
curled-leaf: A tapering leaf whose tip curls into a tight spiral, with a pale midrib line running along its length.
curled-tentacle: A thick tentacle coiled into an inward spiral, lined along its inner edge with rounded suckers, evoking octopus or kraken monsters.
curling-stone: A rounded curling stone with a band across its middle and an angled handle mounted on top.
curling-vines: A tangle of tapering vine tendrils curling into spirals and hooks, spreading outward from a central knot.
curly-mask: An oval face mask split vertically into light and dark halves, with mirrored curling brows, almond eyes and curved mouths, in the manner of theatrical comedy-tragedy masks.
curly-wing: A stylized wing of long tapering feathers sweeping upward, ending at its base in two spiral scroll curls.
cursed-star: A jagged five-pointed star formed of splintered shards, with a slit eye and vertical pupil at its center.
curvy-knife: A curved dagger with a crescent-shaped blade tapering to a point, its segmented grip ending in a rounded pommel.
custodian-helmet: A tall domed British police custodian helmet with a brim and a small crest at the top, bearing a star badge with a central disc and crown.
cut-diamond: A brilliant-cut diamond seen from the front, its flat crown of angled facets above a tapering pointed pavilion, a common emblem of wealth and treasure.
cut-lemon: A lemon sliced across, showing the segmented pulp wedges radiating from the center within the rind, with the tapered whole body behind.
cut-palm: An open hand with fingers spread, split by a jagged gash across the palm, with a single drop falling below it.
cyber-eye: A sphere bearing an eye-shaped iris and pupil at one side, with circuit-board traces ending in oval nodes tracing across the rest of its surface.
cyborg-face: An oval head with a mechanical eye plate and slotted panel on one side, a simple eye on the other, and a slit mouth, depicting a cyborg's face.
cycle: Two thick curved arrows chasing each other in a ring, the standard sign for recycling, refreshing or a repeating cycle.
cycling: A cyclist crouched low over the handlebars of a racing bicycle, shown in side view with both wheels visible.
cyclops: An oval head shape filled almost entirely by a single large eye with iris and pupil, the mark of a cyclops or one-eyed giant.
cz-skorpion: A compact machine pistol in side profile, with a curved magazine, pistol grip, trigger guard and a folded wire stock over its receiver.
d10: A ten-sided die seen from above, its kite-shaped faces marked with the numerals 0, 2, 8, 3 and 7.
d12: A twelve-sided die seen face-on, its central pentagon marked 12 and surrounding faces numbered 2, 8, 4, 6 and 11, a staple of tabletop role-playing games.
d4: A solid triangle bearing the numeral 4 at its apex and rotated numerals 1 and 2 at its lower corners, depicting a four-sided die.
daemon-pull: A human figure with arms flung upward being dragged down by a huge fanged maw rising from below, a depiction of a soul seized by a demon.
daemon-skull: A horned demonic skull with slanted crescent eye sockets, a triangular nose cavity and a grid of bared teeth.
dagger-rose: A dagger with a pommel and curling tendril hilt, its blade thrust diagonally through a spiral rose bloom with leaves.
daggers: Three matching daggers with leaf-shaped blades, fullered centers, winged crossguards set with a round gem, and straight pommeled grips, the outer two tilted inward.
daisy: A many-petalled daisy-like flower with a small oval center, on a curving stem bearing two broad leaves and two smaller ones.
dam: A cross-section of a dam wall holding back a high body of water on one side, with a lower rippling water level on the other.
damaged-house: A house with a chimney, split down the middle by a jagged crack that breaks its roof and walls into separated halves.
dandelion-flower: A round central disc surrounded by a ring of long tapering petals radiating outward, forming a dandelion-like bloom.
dango: Three round dumpling balls of increasing size skewered on a diagonal stick, the Japanese dango sweet.
dark-squad: Three standing figures grouped together, each with an oval head marked by two rectangular eye slits and a long robed body.
dart: A throwing dart angled diagonally, with two curved fletching vanes at the rear, a segmented barrel, and a long tapering needle point.
database: A stack of three cylindrical discs forming a drum shape, the standard symbol for a database or data storage.
dead-eye: A dark eyeball with spiraling iris rings, ringed by a circle bearing eight radiating diamond and cross points like a compass rose or targeting reticle.
dead-head: An oval head with X-shaped eyes and a frowning mouth with the tongue hanging out, the cartoon convention for death or unconsciousness.
dead-wood: A leafless tree with a gnarled trunk splitting into jagged, spiky bare branches, an emblem of blight, decay, or a withered wasteland.
deadly-strike: A humanoid silhouette shown in negative against a burst of long tapering spikes radiating outward behind it, suggesting an explosive impact.
death-juice: A skull with slanted eye sockets and jagged lower jaw, with a single droplet falling below it, a common mark for poison or lethal venom.
death-note: An angular skull with jagged teeth hovering above an open book, a common emblem of necromancy or deadly forbidden knowledge.
death-skull: A broad human skull with round eye sockets, a pointed nasal cavity and a blocky jaw, the standard emblem of death.
death-star: A sphere split by a horizontal equatorial trench, with a large circular dish crater near the top and jagged blocky notches along its right edge, the Death Star battle station.
death-zone: A skull with hollow eye sockets, triangular nose and gritted teeth rising from a flat elliptical ring or disc encircling its base.
deathcab: A mushroom whose domed cap bears a skull face with slanted eyes, small nose and gapped teeth, marking it as a deadly poisonous toadstool.
decapitation: A headless standing figure with its severed oval head tumbling above, a curved sweeping arc marking the blade's slicing path.
deer: A standing stag in profile with branching antlers, head turned and legs braced.
deer-head: A front-facing stag's head with wide flaring ears, slanted eyes, a small muzzle, and tall curving antlers sweeping up from the brow.

defensive-wall: A crenellated fortress wall in three bands: a battlement of square merlons, a stone-block course, and a base of angled buttress supports.

deku-tree: A broad tree with a spreading canopy and thick flared roots, its trunk bearing a face-like pattern of eyes and a pointed nose.
delicate-perfume: A faceted perfume bottle on a flat base, topped with a nozzle and a curving tube leading to an oval squeeze bulb atomizer.
delighted: A face made of two four-pointed star eyes above a wide crescent grin with jagged pointed teeth, in the manner of a carved jack-o'-lantern.
delivery-drone: A quadcopter drone seen head-on, with a central ring-lensed camera body, two rotor bars on posts above, and angled landing legs ending in round feet.
demolish: A crenellated castle tower whose base is broken apart by a jagged zigzag crack and bursting shards of rubble.
dervish-swords: Two crossed curved scimitars with pommeled grips and flared crossguards, their broad blades sweeping downward into a wide arc.
desert: A desert scene with two saguaro cacti rising from a solid ground band beneath a sun disc with radiating rays.
desert-camp: A canvas awning slung between two poles, with a half-disc sun above, a diagonally striped square mat at left and a rounded waterskin at right.
desert-eagle: A semi-automatic pistol seen in side profile, with a long slide, front and rear sights, trigger guard and a grip marked by two round pin holes.
desert-skull: A horned bovine skull seen from the front, with curling horns, oval eye sockets and a notched muzzle, a common emblem of deserts and death.
deshret-red-crown: The deshret, the ancient Egyptian red crown of Lower Egypt, with its tall back spike and curling spiral coil rising from the front, a mark of pharaonic royalty.
desk: A desk with a flat top, a drawer stack on one side and a slanted brace leg on the other, holding a monitor on a stand and a small upright box.

despair: A hunched figure kneeling with head bowed low to the ground, backed by a row of vertical prison-like bars.
detonator: A boxy plunger detonator with a T-shaped handle above the body, marked with a warning triangle enclosing an exclamation point, and flanked by two small rectangles.
detour: A diagonal arrow pointing to the upper right whose shaft loops in a curve around a solid filled circle, the standard sign for bypassing an obstacle.
devil-mask: A horned demonic face mask with two large curving outer horns, two small inner horns, slanted eyes and a fanged grin tapering to a pointed chin.
dew: A leaf with a droplet resting at its tip and a second larger droplet falling below it.
diablo-skull: A horned demonic skull with slanted eyes, a jagged nose, and pointed fangs below, topped by a teardrop shape and flanked by curling horns.
diagram: A sine-like wave curve crossing a dashed horizontal axis at a marked center dot, with short tick lines marking the crest and trough amplitudes.
dial-padlock: A round padlock with a shackle at top, its face bearing a circular combination dial marked with radiating tick marks.
diamond-hard: A large faceted gemstone with a pickaxe swinging above it, small impact marks flying off where the point strikes.
diamond-hilt: A sword hilt seen from the front, with a domed pommel, wrapped grip, diamond-shaped centerpiece, and wide crossguard flaring into diamond-tipped quillons, above the blade's base.
diamond-ring: A thick circular band topped by a faceted gemstone with a flat crown and pointed base, the conventional engagement ring.
diamond-trophy: A faceted brilliant-cut gem mounted on a short stem atop a wide trapezoidal plinth bearing a blank plaque, forming an award trophy.
diamonds: A four-pointed diamond with concave curving sides, the playing-card diamond suit symbol.
diamonds-smile: A face made of two spiral-ringed eyes above a wide grin of large faceted, gem-like teeth.
dice-eight-faces-eight: An octahedral die seen point-down, its large front triangular face marked 8 with neighbouring faces showing 5, 1 and 7.
dice-fire: A six-sided die shown in three-quarter view, its top, left and right faces pipped, set against a rounded mass of flames.
dice-shield: A rounded shield bearing a six-sided die shown in three-quarter view, with three pips on the top face and two on each side face.

dice-target: A six-sided die shown in three-quarter view, centered in a crosshair reticle ring with four tick marks.
dice-twenty-faces-one: A twenty-sided die seen face-on, its central triangular face showing the number 1 with surrounding faces numbered 2, 8, 9, 4, 16, 19 and 15.
dice-twenty-faces-twenty: A twenty-sided die seen face-on with numbered triangular faces, the central one showing 20, the natural-twenty roll of tabletop role-playing games.
dig-dug: A shovel and a pickaxe crossed over each other, the common emblem of mining and excavation.

fairy: A butterfly-like winged form with rounded spots on each wing and a crescent moon marking its round body.
fairy-wand: A slender wand tipped with a five-pointed star, surrounded by scattered four-pointed sparkles, the usual shorthand for magic or enchantment.
fairy-wings: Eight tapered petal-like blades radiating symmetrically from a central point, forming two mirrored sets of wings.
falcon-moon: A bird of prey with outstretched wings and hooked beak flying across a crescent moon.

falling: A human figure tumbling head-downward with limbs splayed, its round head at the lower left, depicting a fall.

falling-bomb: An aerial bomb seen nose-down with tail fins, flanked by tapering speed streaks that convey its rapid descent.
falling-boulder: A large downward-pointing arrow with a circular stone trailing upward flame-like spikes superimposed on it, indicating something plummeting from above.
falling-eye: A round eyeball with a ringed iris and pupil, trailing streaming flame-like strands behind it as it plummets.
falling-leaf: A curled, tapering leaf with a central midrib and angled side veins cut through it, drifting on its side.
falling-ovoid: A burst of jagged spikes trailing to the upper left, with an oval and a crescent shape set within the mass, suggesting a plummeting meteor or comet impact.
falling-rocks: A steep cliff face or slope with angular boulders and small stones tumbling down alongside it, the standard rockslide hazard sign.
falling-star: A five-pointed star with three diagonal streak lines trailing behind it, depicting a shooting star.

famas: A bullpup assault rifle angled diagonally, showing its carry-handle sight rail, trigger guard, magazine and barrel with dashes marking the muzzle line.
family-house: A two-storey house with a wide overhanging roof, a peaked central gable dormer, square windows, and an arch-topped front door.
family-tree: A genealogy chart of solid rectangles linked by bracket-shaped connector lines, four boxes joining into two and then into one below.
fanged-skull: A menacing skull with a domed cranium, angular eye sockets, a jagged nose cavity and a row of teeth flanked by long pointed fangs.
fangs: A set of pointed teeth in upper and lower rows, dominated by two long curved fangs, an emblem of vampires and predatory beasts.
fangs-circle: A circular ring formed by upper and lower rows of long pointed fangs meeting in a gaping maw, an emblem of monstrous beasts.
farm-tractor: A tractor seen from the side, with a large rear wheel, smaller front wheel, canopy roof, and exhaust stack puffing smoke.
farmer: A standing figure in a wide-brimmed hat, one hand on the hip and the other holding an upright three-tined pitchfork.

fat: A heavyset human figure with an oval head, a broad rounded torso, short arms sloping down at the sides, and stubby legs.
feather: A curved plume feather with a slender tapering quill and split, notched vanes along its shaft, the traditional emblem of quill writing and lightness.

feline: A cat in profile walking with an arched back and curled raised tail, its pointed ear and eye picked out in white.

fencer: A masked fencer lunging forward on a horizontal ground bar, rear arm extended back and sword thrust out ahead.
fern: A single curving fern frond with tapered leaflets branching off either side of its central stem.
fertilizer-bag: A bulging sack with crimped top and bottom seams, its face bearing a large upward-pointing arrow with a two-leaved sprouting seedling superimposed on it.

fez: A truncated-cone fez hat seen at an angle, with a tassel cord looping over its flat top and hanging down the side.
field: A circular scene showing a dark plowed field behind a post-and-rail fence, with clouds streaking across the sky above.
field-gun: A wheeled artillery piece seen from the side, its barrel angled upward and a long trail leg resting on the ground behind the spoked wheel.
figurehead: A ship's figurehead of a woman with streaming hair and outstretched arm, mounted on the planked prow of a wooden hull.

finch: A small perching bird in profile with a short pointed beak, long swept-back wing and tail, standing on two clawed feet.

fire-bomb: A round bomb with a curling fuse, marked with a flame cut out of its body.

menhir: A tall upright standing stone, tapering to a rounded point, its right edge broken by jagged chips and cracks.

mesh-ball: A sphere formed of crossing latitude and longitude bands, a woven globe or wireframe ball.
mesh-network: A cluster of dots of varying sizes joined by curved lines into an interconnected web, the common emblem for networks and linked connections.
metal-bar: A trapezoidal metal ingot seen in three-quarter view, its slanted front face marked with angular highlight streaks.
metal-boot: A tall armored boot with a plated shin, riveted toe cap and studded panels, standing on a flat ground bar.
metal-detector: A metal detector with an armrest handle, angled shaft and flat oval search coil, with curved arcs beneath it suggesting emitted waves.
metal-disc: A tilted oval disc crossed by diagonal slashes that extend past its left rim as short streaks, suggesting a spinning thrown disc.
metal-golem-head: A riveted metal head and shoulders with angular slit eyes, jagged sawtooth mouth, bolt-like protrusions at each side, and a split plated chest.
metal-hand: A raised hand with segmented, plated fingers and thumb, the joints split into separate armored bands, like a gauntlet or mechanical hand.
metal-plate: A square armor plate crossed by diagonal bands, with hinge tabs or riveted flanges projecting along its left edge.
metal-scales: Overlapping angular armor plates arranged in tapering rows, forming a scale-mail panel with slotted notches.
metal-skirt: A segmented armor skirt or faulds with a belted waist plate bearing a rectangular buckle, banded side panels, and a long pointed central tasset.
meteor-impact: A round meteor with streaking trail lines behind it striking the ground, which bursts outward in radiating spikes of debris.
metroid: A domed jellyfish-like creature with three round nuclei under its translucent shell and four curved fangs or tendrils hanging beneath, the Metroid of video-game fame.
metronome: A pyramid-shaped mechanical metronome with a graduated scale and a swinging pendulum arm tilted to the left with its weight, plus a winding key at the side.
mexico: A silhouette map of Mexico, with the narrow Baja California peninsula separated along the northwest coast and the hooked Yucatán at the southeast.
microchip: A tilted square integrated-circuit chip with rows of pins along two opposite sides and a marking notch line inside its body.
microphone: A handheld microphone tilted diagonally, with a round ball head, tapered collar bearing a slot, and a short cable curling from the handle's base.
microscope: A microscope in side view, its segmented angled eyepiece tube and objective rising from a stage and heavy stepped base, with a ring-shaped focus knob.
microscope-lens: A thick ring with radiating tick marks around it, enclosing an inward-coiling spiral that ends in a small solid dot.
mid-summit: A steep mountain slope rising to a sharp peak, with a flag on a pole planted on a ledge partway up.
middle-arrow: An arrow driven diagonally through a jagged starburst, its shaft passing through a hole in the center and its fletching and barbed head protruding on either side.
midnight-claw: A black disc gouged by white slash marks forming a splayed three-toed claw print with hooked talons.
mighty-boosh: A rounded ghost-like head with two mismatched round eyes and a large dark gaping mouth showing a row of gritted teeth.
mighty-force: A figure with arms raised and fists clenched in a flexing pose, backed by a fan of radiating flame-like spikes, conveying surging strength or power.
mighty-horn: A large curved animal horn, broad at the base and tapering to a jagged, zigzag-notched tip.
mighty-spanner: A toothed gear ring with a wrench head and angled handle set within it, backed by a jagged starburst of radiating spikes.
military-ambulance: A side view of a boxy truck with two wheels, a sloped cab window, and a circled cross on its cargo body marking it as a medical vehicle.
military-fort: A fortified building with a gateway arch and slit windows below a wide eave, flanked by two small towers, with a circle enclosing three stacked chevrons above.
milk-carton: A gabled milk carton with its pouring spout peaked at the top, its front panel bearing a horned cow's head.
millenium-key: An ankh-shaped key tilted diagonally, with a looped head, crossbar, and a notched shaft ending in a key tooth.
mimic-chest: A treasure chest with a gaping mouth full of jagged fangs, two curling horn-like protrusions on its lid and a keyhole plate on its front, the classic mimic monster.
mine-explosion: A jagged starburst of spiky shards erupting upward from a small dome, with debris streaks flying outward, depicting a buried mine detonating.
mine-truck: A heavy dump truck in side view with two large wheels, a cab window, and a heaped load of ore or rock mounded in its tilting bed.
mine-wagon: A tapered mine cart on two round wheels, heaped with a mound of ore or coal above its rimmed top edge.
minefield: A rectangular sign on a post bearing a skull and crossbones, standing among scattered flat oval shapes on the ground.
miner: A hunched figure swinging a pickaxe into rock, with shards bursting outward from the impact.
mineral-heart: An angular heart shape built from sharp straight edges, with nested outlines forming a maze-like groove tracing its interior.
mineral-pearls: Five scattered rounded pebble-like beads, each marked with a slanted crescent highlight suggesting glossy pearls.
minerals: A cluster of angular gem crystals jutting upward, surrounded by four-pointed sparkles indicating glitter or magical enchantment.
mini-submarine: A small submersible craft in profile with a canopy, periscope mast and a large rear propeller ring, with bubbles rising above it.
minigun: A rotary machine gun seen from the side, with a boxy body, ridged multi-barrel assembly, and ammunition belts curving down from an attached feed box.
mining: A pickaxe swung into a jagged rock face, splitting the stone with cracks and flying chips.
mining-helmet: A hard hat seen from the side with ridged crown bands, a broad brim, and a cylindrical lamp mounted on the front.
minions: A group of four featureless humanoid figures with slit eyes, one large one looming behind three smaller ones, suggesting a leader with followers.
minotaur: A hulking horned bull-headed humanoid seen from the front, with broad shoulders, muscular arms curling inward, and thick legs, depicting the minotaur of myth.
miracle-medecine: A syringe with ringed finger grips and plunger, set against jagged starburst flashes radiating behind it.
mirror-mirror: A rectangular framed mirror with arched top and bottom edges, its face crossed by diagonal bands suggesting reflected glare.
misdirection: A scattered cluster of arrows of varying sizes pointing in many conflicting directions.
missile-launcher: A finned missile angled upward on a rail resting atop a tripod-style stand with splayed legs and footplates.
missile-mech: A bipedal walker robot with a round cockpit body and two angled shoulder pods perforated with circular missile launch tubes, standing on two thick legs.
missile-pod: Three pointed missiles launching in a diagonal row from a solid triangular block, each rocket trailing a curved arc of exhaust.
missile-swarm: A cluster of finned rockets flying diagonally, some large and some small with curving exhaust trails behind them.
mite: A mite or tick seen from above, with a large round body, small segmented head bearing two pincers, and eight curved tapering legs splayed outward.
mite-alt: A round-bodied spider or mite seen from above, with two large eyes, curved fangs below, and eight sweeping legs fanning out to the sides.
moai: A moai head in profile, the Easter Island stone statue with heavy brow, long nose, jutting chin and elongated ear.
modern-city: A cluster of three buildings: a low block with rows of windows and a rooftop antenna, a tall tower with grid windows, and a skyscraper with a slanted top.
moebius-star: A six-pointed star formed from three interwoven angular bands that loop through one another in an impossible endless knot.
moebius-trefoil: Three interlocking crescent arcs arranged in a pinwheel, each ending in a ringed circle, around a solid central dot.
moebius-triangle: A Penrose triangle, the impossible three-beam figure whose sides join in a way no solid object could, a classic optical illusion.
moka-pot: A moka stovetop coffee pot with faceted tapering upper and lower chambers, an angular side handle, a spout, and a small knob on its lid.
moldova: The angular silhouette of Moldova's national territory, a country map outline tapering to a point at the south.
mole: A mole's head seen from the front, with a pointed star-nosed snout and whiskers, flanked by two large clawed digging paws beneath an arched dome of earth.
molecule: A large solid circle overlapped by three smaller circles at its upper, lower, and right edges, the standard cluster used to depict a molecule or atom group.
molotov: A tilted bottle with a burning rag stuffed in its neck, pouring a stream of liquid that erupts into flames, depicting a Molotov cocktail.
mona-lisa: A framed portrait painting of a seated long-haired woman with folded arms, in the pose of the Mona Lisa.
moncler-jacket: A quilted puffer jacket with a high collar, long sleeves and horizontal padded segments across the body.
money-stack: A stack of banknotes seen at an angle, bound by a wrapper band across the middle, each bill marked with an oval center medallion.
mongolia: A solid silhouette of the country of Mongolia's territorial outline, wide and irregular with a small peak along its upper edge.
monk-face: A bust of a hooded man with heavy brows, mustache and chin tuft, wearing a robe marked with a cross on the chest.
monkey: A front-facing monkey head with large round ears, wide eyes, tufted spiky hair, a protruding muzzle and two visible front teeth.
monkey-wrench: A pipe wrench with a long diagonal handle, adjusting screw collar, and hooked upper jaw at the head.
mono-wheel-robot: A robot with a two-eyed rounded head, wide tapering torso with chest slots, thin curving arms ending in pronged claws, and a single segmented wheel below.
monster-grasp: A clawed beast's hand reaching forward with hooked talons spread wide, evoking a monster's grasping attack.
monstera-leaf: A broad heart-shaped monstera leaf with deep slits cutting inward from its edges toward the central midrib.
monument-valley: A flat-topped desert mesa rising from a sloping talus base, with a smaller butte beside it and a round sun or moon in the sky.
moon: A filled disc with a crescent-shaped sliver cut out of its left side, depicting a waning moon within a circle.
moon-bats: A crescent moon with two bats flying across it, a classic emblem of night, Halloween and vampiric horror.
moon-claws: A solid disc gouged by four tapering claw slashes, combining a full moon with rending claw marks, an emblem of werewolves.
moon-orbit: A large solid sphere encircled by a slanted elliptical orbit ring, with a smaller ringed sphere riding along that path.
mooring-bollard: A dockside mooring bollard: a thick post with a wide domed cap, flanked by two horizontal bars, standing on a flat base plate.
morbid-humour: A human skull with large rounded eye sockets, a triangular nose cavity and a wide grinning row of teeth, a common emblem of death.
morgue-feet: A pair of bare feet seen from the soles, with a blank tag hanging over one of them, the standard sign of a corpse in a morgue.
morph-ball: A sphere divided by three curved spiral seams that swirl outward from a small ringed core at its center.
mortar: A mortar artillery piece: an angled tube on a bipod leg with a baseplate, and a finned shell above the muzzle.
mountain-cave: Two peaked mountain outlines drawn as sweeping lines, with a solid dome-shaped cave mouth at the base of the taller peak.
mountain-climbing: A climber hanging from a steep overhanging rock face, gripping the edge with one arm while a rope trails down below.
mountain-road: Two snow-capped mountain peaks with a winding road or river snaking down between them toward the viewer.
mountains: A circular frame enclosing three jagged mountain peaks with snow-capped summits.
mountaintop: A circular frame enclosing a jagged mountain peak with a smaller shoulder ridge beside it, its slopes split into light and dark faces.
mounted-knight: A helmeted knight with a plumed crest riding a rearing horse, couching a long lance forward over its head.
mouse: A mouse seen from above with a long curling tail and two large round ears.
mouth-watering: A face made of two slanted leaf-shaped eyes and a wide crescent grin dripping thick drool in falling droplets.
move: A cross of four arrows pointing up, down, left and right from a common center, the standard sign for moving or repositioning an object.
movement-sensor: A dark disc ringed by short radial notches, flanked by two pairs of curved arcs sweeping outward on either side like emitted waves.
mp-40: A submachine gun seen from the side, tilted diagonally, with a long barrel, downward-angled magazine, pistol grip and folding stock strut.
mp5: A submachine gun seen at an angle, with long barrel shroud, pistol grip, magazine, and detached stock and sight pieces floating nearby.
mp5k: A compact submachine gun in side profile, with pistol grip, curved box magazine, foregrip and rear stock stub.
mucous-pillar: A thick vertical column formed of tapering, lens-shaped strands that bulge and split apart in the middle, resembling stretched strands of slime.
mug-shot: A bust-length silhouette of a person facing forward, holding a placard with text bars, against a background of horizontal height-chart lines, as in a police booking photo.
multi-directions: A solid disc bearing four triangles pointing up, down, left and right around a central ring with a small dot, in the manner of a directional pad or compass rose.
multiple-targets: Four targeting reticles of different sizes and styles: two crosshair rings, a circle framed by corner brackets, and a dashed crosshair, as in a weapon's target-acquisition display.
mummy-head: A head wrapped in overlapping bandage strips, leaving narrow slits for glaring eyes and a jagged-toothed mouth.
muscle-fat: A stocky figure with a featureless oval head flexing both arms upward, showing broad bulky shoulders, a wide torso and short thick legs.
muscle-up: A muscular figure with a small head, broad torso and both arms raised overhead with bulging biceps flexed, a common emblem of strength.
muscular-torso: A heavily muscled male torso seen from the front, with defined pectorals, shoulders, and rows of abdominal muscles, headless and cut off at the waist.
mushroom: A mushroom with a broad domed cap, its underside notched with gill slits, above a short thick stem.
mushroom-cloud: A billowing mushroom cloud rising on a flared stem encircled by a ring of debris, the standard emblem of a nuclear explosion.
mushroom-gills: A broad-capped mushroom seen from below, its wide dome above a thick stalk with gill ridges marked under the cap's underside.
mushroom-house: A cottage built from a mushroom, its spotted cap forming the roof over a gilled band, with a paned window and an arched door in the stalk.
mushrooms: A cluster of three mushrooms with broad domed caps and short thick stems, one large and two smaller ones flanking it.
mushrooms-cluster: A cluster of tall pointed-cap mushrooms with slender stalks rising from a common mound at the base.
music-spell: A single eighth note with a doubled curving flag, set within a broken circular ring.
musical-keyboard: An electronic keyboard seen at a diagonal angle, its row of keys along one edge and control buttons and a knob on the panel above.
musical-notes: Three eighth notes with oval heads and curved flags, the common shorthand for music or song.
musical-score: A treble clef drawn across a five-line musical staff, its tail ending in a filled note head.
musket: A flintlock musket angled diagonally, showing its wooden stock, curved trigger guard, hammer and banded barrel with muzzle at the upper right.
mussel: A mussel shell parted into two elongated oval halves, with the inner flesh shown as a smaller oval between them.
mustache: A bowler hat with a wide brim above a broad handlebar mustache and a pointed goatee, the classic gentleman-disguise emblem.
mute: A face with a raised index finger held vertically across the lips in a "shhh" gesture, the common sign for silence.
nachos: A scattered cluster of six triangular tortilla chips, each marked with small rectangular holes or salt flecks.
nailed-foot: A bare foot and lower leg in profile with a large spike driven down through the top of the foot, its wide head tilted above.
nailed-head: A featureless head-and-shoulders silhouette surrounded by five large nails pointing inward at the skull from above and both sides.
nails: Two long spikes with flat heads and notched, barbed shafts crossed in an X.
nano-bot: A bacteriophage-like machine with two wide angular wings joined by a banded neck, above a central stem flanked by two bent legs.
nautilus-shell: A coiled nautilus shell with banded chambers radiating from its center, with tentacles trailing from the opening at lower left.
neck-bite: A face in profile with narrowed eyes and a wide fanged mouth beside a bare neck and shoulder trickling two drops, the classic vampire bite motif.
necklace: A necklace cord hanging in a loop with a many-pointed star pendant studded with small round gems.
necklace-display: A bust-shaped jewelry display stand wearing a wide collar necklace set with a large oval gem flanked by two small round stones.
nectar: A round fruit or droplet-shaped vessel filled with liquid, topped by a flower with petals and a bud.
needle-drill: A long tapering needle-like drill bit with barbed serrations along one edge and diagonal flutes, set into a broad angular head with a round bore.
needle-jaws: A wedge-shaped maw filled with rows of long interlocking needle-like fangs, suggesting the gaping jaws of a deep-sea predator.
nefertiti: A woman's head in profile wearing a tall flat-topped Egyptian crown with banded stripes, in the manner of the Nefertiti bust and a mark of ancient Egyptian royalty.
nest-birds: Three wide-eyed hatchling birds with open beaks rising from a nest of woven twigs, with small marks radiating around their heads.
nest-eggs: Three eggs resting in a nest woven from crossed twigs and straw.
nested-eclipses: Two concentric crescent shapes, each opening upward, with a small solid disc at the top center, suggesting nested eclipsing spheres.
nested-hearts: A small solid heart centered within a larger heart outline, a conventional emblem of love and affection.
nested-hexagons: A series of concentric hexagon outlines shrinking toward a small solid hexagon at the center.
network-bars: Five vertical bars rising in height from left to right, the standard indicator for signal strength.
new-born: A hatchling chick with open beak emerging from a cracked eggshell whose jagged rim splits across the middle.
new-shoot: A young sprout with a curving stem bearing two broad leaves, rising from a tuft of grass, a common emblem of growth and new life.
newspaper: A spread newspaper seen from above, its two facing pages curving apart and filled with bars of text blocks and rectangular picture panels.
next-button: A right-pointing triangle meeting a vertical bar, the standard skip-forward or next-track control.
nigeria: A solid silhouette map of Nigeria's national borders, with its rounded northern edge and pointed southeastern corner.
night-sky: A circular scene with a crescent moon, a four-pointed star and scattered dots above a jagged mountain silhouette.
night-sleep: A crescent moon with three tilted Z letters rising beside it, the standard shorthand for sleep.
night-vision: A crescent moon above a pair of feline eyes with narrow slit pupils, a common emblem of nocturnal sight.
ninja-armor: A short-sleeved wrap jacket with crossed lapels over a flared skirt, cinched by a sash with a diamond-shaped knot, in the manner of a ninja or martial-arts gi.
ninja-head: A hooded head wearing a masked wrap that leaves only a slitted eye band exposed, with trailing cloth tails behind, the classic ninja disguise.
ninja-heroic-stance: A masked ninja in profile with a long trailing headband, holding a straight sword diagonally across the body.
ninja-mask: An oval hooded head covering with a horizontal light band across the middle showing two narrow slanted eyes, the classic ninja mask.
ninja-star: A four-pointed shuriken with curved, swept blades around a round central hole, the throwing star of ninja lore.
ninja-velociraptor: A raptor dinosaur's head in profile with slit eye, nostril, jaws gaping wide and lined with pointed teeth.
nodular: A vertical stalk topped by a ring and strung with two solid beads of decreasing size, like a knobbed rattle or segmented node chain.
noodle-ball: A solid circular mass sitting atop a tangle of long curving strands that loop and cross beneath it, like a ball of noodles.
noodles: A wide bowl on a small base with three wavy strands rising from it and a pair of chopsticks angled above.
north-star-shuriken: A five-pointed throwing star with arrow-like barbed points and a round hole at its center, a ninja weapon.
nose-front: A human nose seen head-on, with the bridge narrowing upward and the nostril wings and septum outlined at the base.
nose-side: A human nose seen in profile, with the bridge, tip, curved nostril crease and nostril opening marked.
notebook: A spiral-bound notepad tilted at an angle with ruled lines across its page, and a sharpened pencil laid diagonally over it.
nothing-to-say: An oval speech bubble with a tail at its lower left, marked with three small dots in a row, the standard ellipsis for silence or pending speech.
nuclear: A trefoil of three curved blades arranged around a central disc, the standard radiation hazard sign for nuclear or atomic power.
nuclear-bomb: A falling aerial bomb with tail fins, its rounded body marked with the trefoil radiation symbol.
nuclear-plant: Two hourglass-shaped cooling towers venting billowing clouds of steam, the front tower bearing the three-bladed radiation trefoil symbol.
nuclear-waste: Three barrels grouped together, the front one marked with a trefoil radiation symbol, denoting radioactive or toxic material.
nun-face: A woman's face framed by a winged headdress and veil, with a cross marked on the front of her robe.
nunchaku: A pair of nunchaku: two tapered batons joined at their tops by a short chain, splayed apart with cord-wrapped grips near the ends.
nurse-female: A bust of a woman wearing a wide cap marked with a cross, her hair falling at the sides above a uniform with a collar.
nurse-male: A head-and-shoulders bust of a smiling man wearing a cap marked with a cross, the standard emblem of medical care.
o-brick: Four square outlines arranged in a two-by-two grid forming a larger square block.
oak: A broad oak tree with a billowing, lobed canopy above a thick trunk splitting into spreading roots.
oak-leaf: An oak leaf with deeply lobed edges, set diagonally with its stem at the lower right and pale midrib and side veins showing.
oasis: Two palm trees rising behind an oval pool marked with pale streaks suggesting ripples or reflected light.
oat: A grain stalk with paired leaf-like husks along its stem, shown in reverse against a solid circular disc.
obelisk: A tall narrow shaft topped by a separate small pyramid, set above a thin bar and a wide trapezoidal base, forming an obelisk monument.
observatory: An observatory building with a domed roof split open, a telescope barrel protruding skyward from the slit, above a cylindrical base with arched windows.
ocarina: A teardrop-shaped ocarina with rows of oval finger holes and a mouthpiece spout projecting from its narrow end.
occupy: A ruined castle or fortress silhouette with a flag on its tower, fronted by a jagged burst shape holding a tank turret with its gun barrel.
octogonal-eye: An eight-pointed star burst formed from a square and diamond, overlaid by a ring containing a dark eye with a vertical slit pupil, suggesting an all-seeing watcher.
octoman: A standing humanoid figure with a rounded, cross-marked head and several long tapering tentacles splaying out from its back and shoulders.
octopus: An octopus with a large domed head, two round eyes, and curling tentacles spiraling outward.
oden: A diagonal skewer strung with a triangular wedge, a round ball, a small diamond, and a thick rectangular block, the arrangement of a food skewer.
office-chair: A swivel office chair seen from the front, with tall padded backrest, seat cushion, two armrests, and a central post spreading into legs ending in caster wheels.
offshore-platform: An offshore oil rig platform on stilt legs rising from wavy water, topped by a lattice derrick tower, a crane arm, and small deck structures.
ogre: A bald, dome-headed ogre face with pointed ears, heavy brow, wide flat nose and a snarling mouth showing two upward-jutting tusks.
oil-can: An oil can tilted on its side, with a cylindrical body, curved carrying handle, and long bent spout.
oil-drum: A cylindrical barrel seen from above at an angle, banded by two ribs around its body and marked with a small oval bung cap on its lid.
oil-pump: An oil derrick pumpjack with a latticed A-frame tower, tilted walking beam, counterweight, pitman arm and a wellhead block at its base.
oil-rig: A tapering latticed derrick tower on a base bar, with three droplet-like blobs spraying upward from its top.
oily-spiral: A ring outlined in a circle at the center, surrounded by teardrop-shaped droplets curving outward in a swirling pinwheel arrangement.
old-king: A scowling bearded man's face wearing a three-pointed crown, with heavy brows, mustache and a long full beard, depicting an aged king.
old-lantern: An oil lantern with a ring handle on top, curved side guards flanking a bulbous glass globe, and a flared base.
old-microphone: A vintage radio microphone with a ribbed capsule head, held in a U-shaped yoke on a short stand with a flat base bar.
old-wagon: A covered wagon in side view, its ribbed canvas top over a body on two spoked wheels with a projecting tongue, evoking pioneer travel.
olive: An olive sprig with slender pointed leaves spreading from a diagonal stem, with two small oval olives and a leaf near its base.
omega: The Greek letter omega, a thick ring with a gap at the bottom flanked by two flared horizontal feet, conventionally denoting the last or the end.
on-sight: A head-and-shoulders silhouette of a person with wide eyes and raised brows, marked on the chest by a crosshair reticle within a ring.
on-target: An arrow or dart with swept fletching striking the bullseye of a tilted concentric-ringed target, the common sign for accuracy or a goal achieved.
one-eyed: A solid oval head bearing a single eye with a round pupil, beside a cross-shaped scar where the other eye would be.
oni: A horned demon's face with pointed ears, glaring eyes, bared fangs and a grimacing mouth, in the manner of a Japanese oni or hannya mask.
onigori: A rounded triangular rice ball with a notch cut into its base, the classic silhouette of Japanese onigiri wrapped with a strip of seaweed.
open-book: An open book seen from the front, its two facing pages spread wide with curved edges above the sweeping cover beneath.
open-chest: A treasure chest with a domed lid tilted back and a keyhole on its front panel, the standard emblem of loot and hidden riches.
open-folder: A file folder with its front panel tilted forward away from the tabbed back panel.
open-gate: A pair of arched double doors swung outward, each with a narrow slit window, flanked by two upright posts topped with round finials.
open-palm: A hand seen from the side with the palm turned upward and fingers extended, a gesture of offering, giving or receiving.
open-treasure-chest: A treasure chest with its domed lid raised, a keyhole plate on the front, a beaded necklace draped over the side and jagged gems spilling from within.
open-wound: A jagged diagonal gash with ragged, spiked edges and small droplet shapes beside it, depicting a torn slash wound.
opened-food-can: A squat cylindrical tin can with its jagged lid peeled back and curling upward from the rim.
opening-shell: A bivalve shell splitting open into symmetrical curved halves, each divided into tapering segments, with a slim spindle rising between them.
ophanim: A large ring enclosing a smaller eye-like oval, crossed by a slanted band and flanked by small wings, depicting the wheel-angel of biblical lore.
ophiuchus: The Ophiuchus astrological glyph, a U-shaped curve with a wavy stroke crossing over its right arm, marking the serpent-bearer zodiac sign.
oppidum: A hill crowned by a battlemented fortress wall with a gate and a flagless pole, its slope shown as a sweeping shaded curve — a hilltop fortified settlement.
opposite-hearts: Two hearts set diagonally, the upper one pointing down and the lower one inverted to point up.
oppression: A hunched figure kneeling with head bowed low, crushed beneath jagged wedges bearing down from above.
orange: A cross-section slice of a citrus fruit, with wedge-shaped segments radiating around a small round core inside a thick circular rind.
orange-slice: A quarter-round citrus slice with a thick curved rind and four wedge-shaped segments separated by gaps, each marked with a small highlight.
orb-direction: A filled circle with a crescent highlight arc inside, overlaid by a large upward-pointing arrow.
orb-wand: A diagonal wand with a ribbed grip topped by a ring-shaped orb containing two dark circular spots.
orbit: A globe marked with continents, encircled by a ring along which a small sphere travels, the standard sign for a satellite in orbit.
orbital: Two concentric rings with a small filled sphere riding on each, encircling a four-pointed star with a hollow center.
orbital-rays: A solid disc set within a tilted ring, encircled by a swirl of tapering rays radiating outward like a stylized sun or orbiting body.
orc-head: A front-facing orc head with large pointed ears, scowling brows, round eyes, a topknot of hair, and a wide grimacing mouth.
ore: A cluster of angular rock chunks and mineral facets with two four-pointed sparkles beside them, indicating a valuable ore vein.
organigram: An organizational chart: one head-and-shoulders figure at the top linked by branching lines down to three identical figures below, denoting hierarchy or a chain of command.
orrery: A large central sphere with three smaller spheres on bent arms extending from curved base supports, a model of planets orbiting a sun.
ostrich: A running ostrich in profile, with a long curving neck, small beaked head, plumed tail and two striding legs.
otamatone: An eighth note whose oval head bears two small eyes, giving the musical note a face like the Otamatone toy instrument.
ouroboros: A serpent curled into a ring, its fanged head biting its own tail, the ouroboros emblem of eternal cycles and rebirth.
outback-hat: A wide-brimmed bush hat seen at an angle, its crown circled by a band of toothed or studded trim.
over-infinity: Two large diamonds side by side, each with an angular V-shaped notch cut through it, with a small upright oval floating above the point where they meet.
overdose: Three two-toned capsule pills scattered at different angles, each with one half dark and the other light.
overdrive: A toothed gear with a diagonal needle across its hub, encircled by curved swirling blades forming a spinning vortex.
overhead: A curving arrow arcing up and over from the left, then sweeping down to a large triangular arrowhead pointing at the lower right.
overkill: A thick ring enclosing a face with two angled crescent eyes forming a scowling, angry glare.

pressure-cooker: An electric pressure cooker seen from the front, with a domed lid and handle on top, side handles, and a control panel showing a display screen and four buttons.
pretty-fangs: An upper jaw arch with two long curved fangs flanking smaller blocky teeth, an emblem of vampires and other biting monsters.
pretzel: A looped, knotted pretzel with two crossing arms and a trailing tail, with a small separate flake beside it.
previous-button: A left-pointing triangle set against an upright bar, the standard media control for skipping to the previous track.
price-tag: A tilted rectangular tag with a rounded eyelet hole and looping string, marked with a dollar sign.
primitive-necklace: A looped cord knotted at the top and strung with pointed teeth or claws and small beads along its lower curve, a tribal trophy ornament.
primitive-torch: A rough wooden stick angled diagonally with flames flaring from its upper end, a torch.
prism: A triangular prism split ting an incoming beam into a fanned spray of rays, with a four-pointed sparkle above, the classic emblem of refracted light.
prisoner: A hooded figure gripping vertical bars with both hands, seen from the front behind a row of prison bars.
private: A single upward-pointing chevron with slightly curved arms, the military rank insignia of a private.
private-first-class: A single upward-pointing military chevron with a curved lower edge, a rank insignia worn on a uniform sleeve.
processor: A square microchip die with circuit traces radiating outward to dots and terminal pads, the standard emblem of computing hardware.
profit: Three curved arrows converging downward into the open mouth of a money sack, a common emblem of income or gain.
progression: A bar chart of four rising columns with a curved arrow sweeping upward across them, the standard sign for growth or increasing progress.
propeller-beanie: A billed cap with a segmented dome, topped by a short stem carrying a two-bladed propeller.
protection-glasses: A pair of wide safety goggles seen from the front, with a wraparound lens marked by streaks of glare and short side arms.
pschent-double-crown: The pschent, the combined white and red double crown of ancient Egypt, with its tall bulbous cone and curling spiral wire at the front.

pterodactylus: A flying pterodactyl in side view with spread wings, a long beaked head with backward crest, and clawed feet trailing below.

public-speaker: A figure with both arms raised standing behind a tapered lectern with a microphone, on a stage platform.
pull: A figure braced with bent knees hauling on a horizontal rope or bar, with effort lines radiating from its head.
pulley-hook: A teardrop-shaped pulley block with a large ringed axle and a small stud, slung from two angled cables with a curved lifting hook below.

pumpkin: A pumpkin formed of tall vertical lobes flanking a large central bulge, topped by a short curved stem.
pumpkin-lantern: A carved jack-o'-lantern pumpkin with a curved stem, a triangular eye, a round eye, and a wide jagged grin, an emblem of Halloween.

punch: A clenched fist seen head-on from the knuckle side, with four curled fingers and the thumb tucked along the edge.
punch-blast: A clenched fist seen from the knuckles, drawn as white bars against a spiky impact burst, the comic-book sign of a landed blow.

puppet: A jointed marionette-like figure with a round head, oval torso, and detached limb segments ending in ball hands and feet, arms raised outward.
purple-tentacle: A broad tapering tentacle with two raised arm-like limbs, its front bearing a row of three oval suckers and a small eye at the tip.
push: A hunched figure leaning forward with both arms braced against a large curved block, straining to shove it, with effort lines bursting above the head.
puzzle: An assembled cluster of interlocking jigsaw puzzle pieces with one piece missing at the lower center, leaving a gap.
pylon: An electricity transmission tower with splayed lattice legs, two horizontal crossarms, and twin peaked tips at the top.

pyromaniac: A grinning bust of a person with narrowed eyes, silhouetted against a background of licking flames that surround the head like hair.
qaitbay-citadel: A symmetrical stone fortress with crenellated corner towers, a taller central turret with arched openings, square windows and an arched gateway.
quake-stomp: A heavy laced boot slamming down onto ground that splits into jagged cracks, with short impact lines flying out to either side.
queen-crown: A crown with four spikes tipped by balls, three round gaps between them, resting above a separate horizontal bar, an emblem of royalty.

quicksand: A wide-eyed figure with arms flung upward sinking into concentric rings of a pit, depicting someone swallowed by quicksand.
quill: A single feather with a split, tapering shaft and barbs notched into separate segments, the classic quill pen of writing and scribes.
quill-ink: A feather quill standing in a wide-based inkwell with a flat rim, the classic emblem of writing and scribes.
quiver: A tapered quiver with a shoulder strap looping from its mouth to its tip, holding several fletched arrows that jut from the top.
rabbit: A rabbit seated in profile with long ears swept back, a small round eye, and a short upturned tail.
rabbit-head: A front-facing rabbit head with two long upright ears, round eyes, a small triangular nose and a smiling muzzle.
raccoon-head: A raccoon's face seen head-on, with pointed ears, a dark bandit mask around round eyes, a small nose and a muzzle.
race-car: A vintage open-cockpit roadster seen from the side, with a small windscreen and two spoked wheels.
radar-cross-section: A circular radar scope with crosshair spokes and an inner ring, overlaid by an irregular angular blob marking a detected target.

radar-sweep: Concentric broken rings around a solid center dot with a tapering bar extending diagonally outward, the standard depiction of a radar screen's sweeping beam.

radial-balance: Eight double-headed arrows arranged in a pinwheel ring around an empty center, each pointing both inward and outward.
radiations: A solid bulging mass at the left emitting three wavy lines, each ending in a small dot, the usual shorthand for radiation or emitted energy.
radio-tower: A tapering lattice mast with cross-braced legs, topped by a dot with curved arcs spreading outward on both sides to indicate broadcast waves.

raft: A raft of lashed logs seen end-on as a row of circles, floating on wavy water with a tattered sail on a mast above.

rail-road: A railroad track seen in perspective, two rails converging toward the horizon with crossties between them and tie ends jutting outside.

rank-1: A shield-shaped banner with a pointed lower edge, bearing a single downward chevron, the insignia of a first military rank.
rank-2: A shield-like pennant with a pointed lower edge bearing two downward-pointing chevrons, a military insignia of rank.
rank-3: A pointed-bottom shield badge bearing a five-pointed star above two downward chevrons, a military insignia of rank.

raven: A perched raven in profile with a heavy pointed beak, round pale eye and long tapering tail, a common omen bird of ill fortune.

razor: A straight razor with its curved handle swung back and the blade extended, pivoting on a riveted hinge.
razor-blade: A double-edged safety razor blade set diagonally, its central slot formed by linked round and oval cutouts.
reactor: A trefoil of three wedge-shaped blades radiating around a central disc, the standard radiation and nuclear hazard sign.
read: A headless figure's rounded head and two circular hands holding up a spread book, seen from the front.

remedy: A stoppered medicine bottle with a wide body and short neck, marked with a cross on its front, the standard sign for medicine or healing.

rice-cooker: A squat pot with a domed lid and knob, side handles, short legs, and a rectangular control panel bearing two switches on its front.

road: A road shown in perspective, its two edge lines converging toward the top with a row of dashed center-line markings shrinking into the distance.

rock-golem: A hulking humanoid figure built from angular stone slabs, with broad shoulders, thick arms and a blocky head showing two slanted eyes.

rocking-chair: A rocking chair seen from the side, with a curved backrest, seat, legs and a long curved rocker runner beneath.

roller-skate: A high-topped boot in side view mounted on a flat bar with four ring-shaped wheels beneath it.

rooster: A standing rooster in profile with a comb, wattle, spurred legs and a plume of arched tail feathers, a traditional emblem of dawn.

saber-slash: A curved saber with a hilt and knuckle guard sweeping upward, trailing a fan of tapering streaks that mark the arc of its swing.
