sausage: A curved link sausage with twisted tie ends at each tip and pale scoring marks along its length.
sausages-ribbon: A ring formed of separate plump sausage-like links arranged end to end in a broken circle, with two small fragments near the gap.
save: A floppy disk with its shutter slot at top, overlaid by a large upward-pointing arrow, the standard sign for saving or uploading data.
save-arrow: A downward-pointing arrow above a horizontal bar, the standard sign for saving or downloading.
saw-claw: A curved claw or talon whose inner edge is cut into jagged saw teeth, tapering to a sharp downward point.
sawed-off-shotgun: A short double-barreled shotgun angled upward, with curved grip, trigger guard and a small separate wedge shape near the stock.
saxophone: A saxophone with curved body, flaring bell, angled mouthpiece and a row of small round keys along its neck.
scabbard: A tapering sheath with a banded throat and hanging strap, angled diagonally with a pommel-topped hilt emerging from its mouth.
scale-mail: A short-sleeved shirt with a rounded neckline, patterned with zigzag chevron rows and a separate band across its hem.
scales: A balance scale with a central column on a wide base and two hanging pans suspended from a level beam, the conventional emblem of justice and fairness.
scallop: A fan-shaped scallop shell with radiating ribs spreading from a narrow hinge, a traditional pilgrim's badge.
scalpel: A scalpel angled diagonally, with a slim grooved handle and a broad curved blade tapering to a fine point.
scalpel-strike: Two long tapering blades angled downward to the right, each paired with a thinner slash line trailing behind it, suggesting swift cutting strokes.
scar-wound: A jagged diagonal gash with ragged, spiked edges branching outward, depicting a torn scar across flesh.
scarab-beetle: A beetle seen from above with a rounded head, two antennae, six splayed legs and an oval striped shell, an emblem of ancient Egypt and rebirth.
scarecrow: A straw-stuffed figure with a round head crowned by spiky tufts, arms stretched wide on a crossbar with straw bursting from tied cuffs and ragged legs.
school-bag: A backpack seen from the front, with a carry loop and two shoulder straps at the top and a large front pocket bearing a T-shaped zipper mark.
school-of-fish: A dense group of overlapping fish with round eyes and gill marks, swimming in rows in alternating directions.
schrodingers-cat-alive: A cat's head, chest and curling tail rising from a box whose flaps are folded out and whose front bears a radiation trefoil.
schrodingers-cat-dead: A box marked with a radiation trefoil, with flaps spread wide, a wisp of vapor rising, and a fanged cat skull emerging above it.
scissors: A pair of scissors with two oval finger loops and spread blades, angled diagonally.
scooter: A motor scooter seen in side profile, with a step-through frame, curved seat, front leg shield, handlebar with mirror, and two spoked wheels.
scorpio: The Scorpio zodiac glyph, an M-like figure whose final stroke curves down and ends in an upward-pointing barbed arrow tail.
scorpion: A scorpion seen from above with a segmented tail curling up over its back and two large pincers extended forward.
scorpion-tail: A scorpion's segmented tail curled upward in a loop and ending in a pointed stinger.
scout-ship: A front view of a spacecraft with a tapering teardrop fuselage, a domed cockpit canopy, and swept curved wings flanking it.
screaming: A figure clutching its head with both hands, mouth wide open in a scream, with radiating rays bursting outward above.
screen-impact: A jagged burst of spikes radiating outward from a star-shaped void at its center, the standard depiction of an explosive impact or shattering blow.
screw: A wood screw seen at an angle, with a slotted rounded head and a tapering threaded shank ending in a point.
screwdriver: A flat-head screwdriver angled across the frame with a ridged handle, flanked by two screws with threaded shafts.
scroll-quill: A sheet of parchment with curled side edges and zigzag lines of writing, crossed diagonally by a feather quill pen.
scroll-unfurled: An unrolled parchment scroll with curled rolls at its top-left and bottom-left corners and ragged torn edges, a stock emblem of spells, decrees, and ancient writings.
scuba-mask: A diving mask with a nose pocket, paired with a curved snorkel tube running up its right side.
scuba-tanks: A pair of upright diving cylinders banded together with straps, with a curving hose looping out from each side.
scythe: A scythe with a long curved blade sweeping to the right and a bent snath crossing down to the lower right, an emblem of harvest and of Death.
sea-cliff: A steep rocky cliff face rising at the right, with a wave splashing against its base and wavy water lines running off to the left.
sea-creature: A long-necked plesiosaur-like head rising from the water with two humps trailing behind it, the classic depiction of a lake monster or sea serpent.
sea-dragon: A serpentine dragon whose horned, long-snouted head rises above a body coiled into a spiral that ends in an arrow-like pointed tail tip.
sea-serpent: The head and S-curved neck of a serpentine dragon with a long fanged snout, spiny crest and round eye.
sea-star: A five-armed starfish with tapering points, marked at its center by a smaller outlined star.
sea-turtle: A sea turtle seen from above and behind, its scute-patterned shell, outstretched flippers, and small head extended forward.
sea-urchin: A round body ringed with long and short tapering spines radiating outward, depicting a sea urchin.
seagull: A seagull standing in profile with a folded wing, tapered tail and short legs on webbed feet, its beak drawn as a separate wedge shape.
seahorse: A seahorse in profile with a long snout, crested head, side fin, and curled prehensile tail.
seated-mouse: A mouse seen from behind, sitting upright with large round ears and a long curling tail, perched on a flat oval ring base.
secret-book: A thick book with its covers together, seen at an angle, bearing a keyhole on a rectangular clasp plate across its front and a ribbon marker at the edge.
secret-door: A dashed outline of an arch-topped doorway with a short horizontal dash for a handle, the standard map notation for a hidden door.
security-gate: A person standing beneath a doorway-shaped archway topped with round lamps, with a small square light flashing beside it, the standard sign for a metal-detector checkpoint.
seedling: A young sprout with a slender curving stem and several leaves rising from a wide-rimmed flower pot.
select: Four thick curved arcs arranged as the corner segments of a broken circle, the standard reticle marking a selected or targeted area.
self-love: A heart outline whose left lobe curls inward and terminates in a large arrowhead pointing back into the heart's center.
sell-card: A rounded rectangular card with an up arrow above it, beside a cinched money bag with a down arrow above it, indicating trading a card for coin.
semi-closed-eye: A wide eye with a large round iris and pale pupil, set within a circular ring formed by curved upper and lower lids.
sensuousness: A stylized human figure with an oval head, tapering limbs and arms outstretched, one raised and one lowered, standing with legs apart as if dancing.
sentry-gun: An automated turret with a boxy body, ammunition magazine on top and a barrel jutting from its side, mounted on a swivel over splayed tripod legs.
sergeant: Three stacked upward-pointing chevrons, the standard rank insignia of a sergeant or other non-commissioned officer.
serrated-slash: A curved crescent-shaped slash mark tapering to a sharp point, its thick inner edge broken by jagged serrated notches, suggesting a claw or blade stroke.
server-rack: A stack of three wide server units, each marked with slots, a narrow indicator and a round light, separated by spacer bars and set on a segmented base.
sesame: A scattering of small pointed oval seeds tilted at varied angles, as of sesame or similar grains.
settings-knobs: Three vertical slider tracks, each crossed by a rounded rectangular handle set at a different height, the standard sign for adjustable settings or controls.
seven-pointed-star: A solid seven-pointed star with short, broad triangular points, the heptagram-like star sometimes used as a mystical or faerie sigil.
severed-hand: A hand with splayed fingers cut off at the wrist, with ragged flesh and a jagged bone stub protruding from the stump.
sewed-shell: A rounded snail-like shell with a spiral whorl, its crack mended by a curving line of stitches beaded along one side.
sewing-machine: A sewing machine seen from the front, with two round dials on its body, a needle bar and presser foot above the flat bed, and a spool pin at the top.
sewing-needle: A sewing needle angled across the frame with a curling thread looping through its eye and winding around it.
sewing-string: A spool wound with thread beside a sewing needle whose eye holds a long wavy strand curving up and over.
sextant: A sextant with its curved graduated arc, index arm, telescope sight and mirror, an instrument of celestial navigation and seafaring.
shadow-follower: A solid standing human figure beside a second identical figure drawn only as a thin outline, suggesting a shadow or ghostly double trailing behind.
shadow-grasp: A clawed hand reaching downward with long splayed fingers curled to grasp, rendered as sweeping tapered strokes.
shaking-hands: Two hands clasped in a handshake, with sleeved forearms extending to either side, a conventional sign of agreement, greeting, or alliance.
shambling-mound: A lumbering humanoid mass of tangled vines, leaves and creepers with jagged eyes and a large flower on its chest, depicting a plant monster.
shambling-zombie: A hunched humanoid figure lurching forward with both arms outstretched and mouth agape, surrounded by scattered small diamond flecks.
shamrock: A three-lobed clover leaf on a curving stem, each lobe marked with a central vein — the emblem of Ireland and of good luck.
shard-sword: A sword angled diagonally with a jagged, shard-like blade of angular spikes, its crossguard tipped with small squares and a straight grip below.
share: Three filled circles joined by straight bars, one node at left linking to two at right, the standard sign for sharing or a network branch.
shark-bite: A shark's head with jaws gaping wide, rows of triangular teeth bared, lunging at a human leg and foot being pulled into its mouth.
shark-fin: A tall curved shark fin rising above two wavy water lines, the classic warning sign of a shark approaching at the surface.
shark-jaws: A shark's pointed snout seen head-on with gaping jaws lined by rows of jagged triangular teeth.
sharp-axe: A double-bladed battle axe with two crescent blades flanking a spiked top and a long diagonal haft.
sharp-crown: A crown with tall sharp spikes and oval gem cutouts, above two narrow leaf-shaped eye slits suggesting a masked face beneath it.
sharp-halberd: A halberd head with a broad curved axe blade and a spike, its diagonal shaft broken into separated segments.
sharp-lips: A gaping maw with curved upper and lower lips lined with rows of long pointed fangs, a monstrous or predatory bite.
sharp-shuriken: A four-pointed throwing star with a round hole at its center, the classic ninja shuriken.
sharp-smile: A menacing face reduced to two slanted leaf-shaped eyes above a wide grin of long jagged fangs, in the manner of a jack-o'-lantern.
sharped-teeth-skull: A horned demonic skull with slanted eye sockets, a flame-shaped nose cavity, and a row of long pointed fangs below.
shatter: A small jagged star at the center surrounded by elongated splinter shards flying outward in all directions, depicting something bursting apart.
shattered-glass: A stemmed wine glass breaking apart, its bowl split by jagged cracks with shards flying off to the side.
shattered-heart: A heart broken apart into several angular fragments separated by jagged gaps, the common emblem of heartbreak or lost love.
shattered-sword: A sword with hilt and crossguard intact but its blade broken into scattered flying fragments.
shears: A pair of garden shears with long tapering blades spread apart above a round central pivot, with thick angled handles below.
sheep: A standing sheep in profile with a thick woolly fleece body, slender legs, ears, and a face showing eyes and teeth.
sheikah-eye: A wide stylized eye with a ringed pupil, flared lash points at both corners and a tapering teardrop spike descending from beneath it, an all-seeing watchful emblem.
shepherds-crook: A shepherd's crook, a staff whose upper end curls into a large hook, with two collar rings banding the lower shaft.
sherlock-holmes: A silhouetted man in profile wearing a deerstalker cap and caped coat with a curved smoking pipe, beside a magnifying glass, the classic detective emblem.
shield: A solid heater-style shield with a peaked top edge and sides tapering to a point at the bottom, a standard emblem of defense and protection.
shield-bash: A running figure charging forward behind a large shield held out at arm's length, with speed streaks trailing behind.
shield-bounces: A shield with a bordered inner field, with four arrowheads deflecting away from it at increasing angles.
shield-disabled: A solid shield crossed by a thick diagonal bar, the standard sign for something negated or deactivated — here protection nullified.
shield-echoes: Three overlapping heater shields stepped diagonally, the frontmost filled solid and the two behind it left as outlines, suggesting a repeating or echoing ward.
shield-impact: A tilted shield with cracks splitting its surface and shards and radiating spikes flying off its upper edge, indicating a violent blow.
shield-opposition: Two tall pointed shields tilted away from each other with a jagged lightning bolt striking down between them.
shield-reflect: A shield struck by a four-pointed starburst impact, with a long arrow bouncing off and flying away to the lower left.
shieldcomb: A pointed heater shield filled with a honeycomb pattern of hexagonal cells.
shining-claw: A single curved talon or claw with light glinting off its inner edge in jagged spark shapes.
shining-heart: A heart with a crescent-shaped highlight, surrounded by long tapering rays bursting outward in all directions.
shining-sword: A sword pointing upward, set against a lens-shaped field with jagged rays bursting outward around the blade.
shinto-shrine: A torii gate with upswept curved crossbeams atop two thick pillars, each flanked by low fence posts and rails, marking a Shinto shrine entrance.
shinto-shrine-mirror: A round disc cradled in a pair of upswept curved arms above a tiered pedestal of stacked bars and a wide base, a Shinto shrine mirror.
shiny-apple: An apple with a curved stem and a crescent-shaped highlight gleaming on its right side.
shiny-entrance: A spiky radiating burst with an arched doorway-shaped opening cut into its base, suggesting a glowing portal or gateway.
shiny-iris: A spiky starburst ring surrounding a crescent-shaped iris with a round pupil, forming a radiant eye.
shiny-omega: A thick ring broken at the bottom, forming the Greek letter omega, surrounded by jagged radiating rays and flanked by two tapering horizontal bars at its base.
shiny-purse: A cinched coin pouch with a flared, ruffled top, set within a white disc ringed by jagged radiating spikes suggesting a burst of light.
ship-bow: The prow of a ship marked with an anchor emblem and a horizontal stripe, cutting through wavy water below.
ship-wheel: A ship's steering wheel with a thick rim studded with round holes, eight spokes radiating to a central hub, and eight tapered handles projecting outward.
ship-wreck: A sailing ship sinking bow-up into wavy water, its tilted mast, tattered sails and broken spars leaning over the surface.
shirt: A long-sleeved tunic or shirt with a V-neck collar, a row of diamond-shaped buttons down the front, and a banded waist hem.
shirt-button: A round button seen face-on, with a thin ring groove inside its rim and four small holes arranged around the center.
shoebill-stork: The head and shoulders of a shoebill stork in profile, with a crest of feathers, round eye, and heavy hooked bill resting against its plumed body.
shooner-sailboat: A two-masted schooner under full sail, its hull below a spread of triangular and quadrilateral sails with a long bowsprit jib.
shop: A storefront building with a scalloped striped awning, a rooftop sign, a large display window and a narrow door beside it.
shopping-bag: A trapezoidal shopping bag widening toward the base, with two round eyelets at the top and a single arched carrying handle.
shopping-cart: A wheeled shopping trolley with a gridded wire basket and an angled push handle, the common sign for shops and purchasing.
shorts: A pair of cargo shorts with a segmented waistband, button fly and patch pockets on each leg.
shotgun: A tall rounded rectangle with a smaller rectangular hole in its upper half, above a separate short horizontal bar.
shotgun-rounds: A group of shotgun shells: one standing upright with crimped top, one lying on its side, and another seen end-on showing its primer ring.
shoulder-armor: A faceted breastplate cuirass with a high spiked collar, flared pauldrons at the shoulders, and banded lames across the abdomen.
shoulder-bag: A narrow tote bag with a rounded body, a horizontal band across its top edge, and a tall arching carry strap.
shoulder-scales: A shoulder pauldron formed of curved, overlapping armor plates arranged in banded rows across a solid mass.
shouting: An egg-shaped head with angry brows and a wide round open mouth, flanked by curved arcs radiating outward like sound waves.
shower: A dome-shaped shower head angled downward, spraying long straight streaks of water diagonally across the field.
shrimp: A curled shrimp seen from the side, with long antennae, a large round eye, segmented body plates, small legs and a fanned tail.
shrug: A standing human figure with an oval head and both arms raised outward with upturned palms in a shrug, the common gesture for ignorance or indifference.
shuriken: A four-pointed throwing star with swept, angled blades around a round central hole, each point marked with a slim highlight stripe; a ninja weapon.
shuriken-aperture: A swirling pinwheel of four curved, tapering blades spiraling around a small solid disc, like a camera aperture caught mid-rotation.
shut-rose: A rose bud on a curling stem that spirals at the base, with two broad leaves and small thorns along the stalk.
shuttlecock: A badminton shuttlecock shown point-up, with a domed cork tip, a banded skirt lattice, and splayed feathers flaring below.
sickle: A sickle with a broad crescent blade curving up from a short banded handle, a harvesting tool also known as a communist emblem.
sideswipe: A broad curving arrow that sweeps around from lower right and points left with a large triangular head, indicating a sideways sweeping motion.
siege-ram: A wheeled battering ram: a wooden frame on two large wheels with a canopy above and a horned ram's-head striking tip projecting from one side.
siege-tower: A wheeled siege tower with a crenellated top platform, cross-braced tapering frame, three round wheels, and a drawbridge ramp lowered from its side.
sight-disabled: An eye with a round pupil crossed out by a thick diagonal slash, the standard sign for hidden, blinded, or disabled vision.
silence: A tilted padlock with a shackle arching above its body, bearing a musical note on its face.
silenced: An oval face with wide eyes and two crossed bandage strips taped over the mouth, the standard sign for enforced silence or muteness.
silex: A chipped flint stone with scalloped edges and curved flake-scar lines across its face, the kind of knapped rock used for Stone Age tools or firestarting.
silver-bullet: A rifle cartridge with pointed tip angled upward, surrounded by scattered four-pointed sparkles, the usual shorthand for magic or enchantment.
sinagot: A two-masted sailing boat with tall triangular sails billowing above a low hull.
sing: An oval head with two arched closed eyes and a wide oval mouth containing a musical note, depicting singing.
sink: A sink basin seen from above with a tall curved faucet spout and two small handles rising behind it.
sinking-ship: An ocean liner tilted bow-up with its row of portholes and three smokestacks angled skyward, sliding stern-first into wavy water.
sinking-trap: A figure with arms flung upward and fingers splayed, its tapering body descending into a small ellipse in the ground, as when sinking into quicksand.
sinusoidal-beam: A broadening diagonal beam shooting from a corner, wrapped by a wavy sinusoidal line that loops alternately above and below it.
siren: A dome-topped emergency light on a flat base, with five straight rays radiating outward to show it flashing, a standard alarm signal.
sitting-dog: A silhouette of a dog seated in profile with a pointed ear, muzzle raised, and a long curved tail sweeping behind it.
six-eyes: Six almond-shaped eyes with round irises and highlights, arranged in two staggered columns, suggesting a many-eyed watching creature.
skateboard: A skateboard seen from beneath at a diagonal angle, showing the deck with its two trucks and four wheels.
skateboarding-01: A stick figure with outstretched arms balanced atop a tilted skateboard, with sharp motion spikes bursting from the board's lower end.
skateboarding-02: A figure with arms outstretched riding a tilted skateboard, with curved motion streaks trailing behind.
skeletal-hand: A skeleton hand splayed open, with separated finger bones, thumb, and carpal blocks at the wrist, an emblem of undead and death.
skeleton: A full human skeleton standing frontally, its skull with two round eye sockets above ribs, spine, pelvis and separated limb bones.
skeleton-inside: A splayed humanoid figure with arms and legs outstretched, its skull, ribcage and limb bones marked as pale segments within the body silhouette.
skeleton-key: A key angled diagonally, its rounded bow shaped like a skull with triangular eye and nose openings and a small ring hole, the shaft ending in notched teeth.
ski-boot: A tall rigid ski boot seen in profile, with buckle straps across the shin and forefoot and a thick flat sole.
skid-mark: A tapering diagonal tire track, its treads marked by zigzag chevron grooves, narrowing to a point at the upper right.
skier: A crouching skier in a downhill tuck, holding poles behind, with a long ski running diagonally beneath and an oval helmeted head detached above.
skills: A person's bust and head in silhouette beside a branching line diagram whose limbs end in three filled circles, the standard layout of a skill tree or org chart.
skimmer-hat: A flat-topped straw boater hat with a wide brim and banded crown, viewed at an angle from above.
skipping-rope: A looped, coiled cord curling into a large loop with a smaller inner loop, its two short straight handles angled at the upper left.
skirt: A flared skirt with a separate straight waistband above it, the fabric falling in broad vertical pleats with an uneven hem.
skis: A pair of skis crossed in an X with upturned tips, standing beside two ski poles with handles and baskets.
skull-bolt: A skull with round eye sockets and jagged teeth trailing a diagonal plume of billowing clouds and scattered dots streaming off to the upper left.
skull-crack: A skull with round eye sockets and a triangular nose, its crown split by a jagged crack with shards flying off above.
skull-crossed-bones: A rounded human skull with round eye sockets, triangular nose and squared teeth, set over four crossed bones, the classic sign of poison, death and piracy.
skull-in-jar: A skull with round eye sockets, triangular nose cavity and a curved grinning jaw, set within a tall dome-topped glass container.
skull-mask: An oval human skull face with slanted eye sockets, a triangular nose and a row of bared teeth, a common emblem of death.
skull-ring: A ring band topped by a skull with round eye sockets and square teeth, with three beads set along its lower edge.
skull-sabertooth: A rounded skull with slanted eye sockets, a triangular nose hole, and three long downward-hanging fangs.
skull-shield: A heraldic shield with a concave-topped edge bearing a large skull with angular eye sockets and jagged, interlocking teeth.
skull-signet: An angular skull with triangular eye sockets, a triangular nose and bar-like teeth, set over stacked elliptical rings that ring it like a band.
skull-slices: A side-view skull with a triangular eye socket and jagged teeth, its cranium formed of concentric crescent bands spiralling inward.
skull-staff: A staff topped with a skull whose teeth are bared, backed by a wide crescent blade, an emblem of necromancy and death magic.
skull-with-syringe: A cracked skull with fangs, overlaid by a syringe whose needle drips a falling droplet, a common sign for poison or lethal injection.
slalom: A winding serpentine arrow curving back and forth between scattered solid dots, ending in an arrowhead at the lower left.
slap: An open hand with spread fingers swinging across a thick crescent arc that curves around it, suggesting the motion of a striking palm.
slashed-shield: A heater shield cut across by several diagonal slash marks, suggesting damaged or broken defenses.
slavery-whip: A hunched figure kneeling on all fours with head bowed as a coiling whip cracks above its back in a burst of impact spikes.
sleeping-bag: A person's head and shoulders emerging from a tapered sleeping bag, surrounded by floating "Z" letters, the standard shorthand for sleep.
sleepy: An oval face with two downturned crescent eyes and a wide yawning mouth, the standard cartoon sign of drowsiness or sleep.
sleeveless-jacket: A sleeveless vest with a rounded collar and front opening, bearing a flapped patch pocket on each side panel.
sleeveless-top: A sleeveless tank top with a deep scooped neckline, narrow shoulder straps, and a waist that nips in before flaring at the hem.
sliced-bread: A loaf of bread cut into several standing slices, with two more slices lying flat in front of it.
sliced-mushroom: Two overlapping mushroom slices cut lengthwise, each showing a rounded cap and tapering stem.
sliced-sausage: A thick sausage with a twisted casing end at one end and a cut face at the other showing rounded fat speckles.
slicing-arrow: A double-headed arrow slashing diagonally, flanked by tapering motion streaks radiating from the lower-right corner to convey rapid slicing movement.
slime: A blob-like slime creature with narrowed eyes, an open mouth and drips running off its spreading base, with a small puddle beside it.
sling: A sling with looped cords and a leather pouch, accompanied by three round stones.
slingshot: A Y-shaped forked slingshot with an elastic band strung between its prongs and a leather pouch pulled back at the top.
slipknot: A hangman's noose: a vertical rope with two binding wraps above a wide teardrop-shaped loop, an emblem of execution and death.
slippers: A pair of slippers seen from above, each split into a rounded toe cap and a separate heel section.
slot-machine: A slot machine cabinet with an arched top, a window showing three vertical reels, a side lever with knob, and a control panel with buttons and an oval.
sloth: A sloth hanging by its long curved limbs from a diagonal branch, its round face turned outward with wide eyes and snout.
slow-blob: A round blob with a hollow circular center, ringed by eight rounded, teardrop-like lobes bulging outward like pseudopods.
slumbering-sanctuary: Six bent bars arranged in mirrored pairs, each angling inward at the top and dropping into vertical stems, forming a symmetrical fan or nested chevron pattern.
sly: A face made of two slanted leaf-shaped eyes above a wide crescent grin with a tongue-like shape below it, giving a sly, mischievous expression.
small-fire: A cluster of curling flame tongues rising together into a fire.
small-fishing-sailboat: A small sailing boat with a hull, two masts and several angular triangular sails spread fore and aft.
smart: A standing human figure whose head is a radiating light bulb with a glowing filament, the common shorthand for a bright idea or sudden insight.
smartphone: A rectangular smartphone seen face-on, with a large blank screen, a slot-shaped earpiece above it and a round button below.
smash-arrows: Three thick parallel arrows pointing straight downward, their heads converging side by side at the bottom.
smitten: An oval face with two heart-shaped eyes and a broad grinning mouth, the standard sign for infatuation or a love charm.
smoke-bomb: A round black bomb with a highlight glint, emitting a large billowing plume of curling smoke that widens upward.
smoking-finger: A hand with the index finger extended, with a curling plume of smoke rising from its tip.
smoking-orb: A low mound or dome with wavy tendrils of smoke curling upward from it in tapering ribbons.
smoking-pipe: A tobacco pipe in side profile, with a deep rounded bowl and a long slender stem angling upward to the mouthpiece.
smoking-volcano: A broad conical volcano with streaks running down its slopes and a billowing cloud of smoke mushrooming above its summit.
snail: A snail in profile with a large spiral shell on its back and two knob-tipped eyestalks rising from its head.
snail-eyes: A snail's head and body with two long stalks rising from it, each tipped with a rounded eye.
snake: A serpent coiled into an S-shaped double curve, its head at the top with a large eye and tapering tail below.
snake-bite: A snake's gaping oval mouth seen head-on, with two curved fangs descending from the upper jaw and slit eyes above.
snake-egg: A cracked egg with jagged fracture lines, a serpent emerging from its side and coiling in an S-curve with its head lowered.
snake-jar: A snake coiled in an S-curve with open jaws, rising above a flat rimmed lid atop a wide hexagonal jar.
snake-spiral: A snake coiled into a flat spiral, its head raised at the outer end with jaws parted and fangs showing.
snake-tongue: A snake with a curving S-shaped body, its head lowered and slit eyes and fangs visible, with a forked tongue flicking out below.
snake-totem: An angular blocky snake head with a round eye and forked tongue extending from its mouth, its body coiling back in sharp zigzag folds.
snatch: A plump drawstring sack with a ruffled gathered neck, set against several long tapering claw-like streaks fanning out behind it as if it were being grabbed away.
sniffing-dog: A dog's head in profile lowered to a horizontal ground line, its nose emitting radiating lines to indicate sniffing.
snitch-quidditch-ball: A small round ball banded with a spiral-tipped strap and flanked by two long feathered wings, the winged golden snitch of Quidditch.
snorkel: A snorkel tube with a ribbed band near the top, curving into a J-shaped mouthpiece with side straps, associated with diving and swimming underwater.
snout: An animal's muzzle seen head-on, with a broad dark nose, whisker dots on both cheeks, and a lower lip line below.
snow-bottle: A round-bodied flask with an angled neck, marked with a large six-armed snowflake on its bulb.
snowboard: A snowboard seen at an angle, its deck marked with two loop-shaped binding straps and a stripe near the tip.
snowflake-1: A six-armed snowflake formed of angular spokes, rendered as pale gaps within a jagged solid hexagonal mass.
snowflake-2: A six-fold snowflake built from hexagonal lobes radiating around a hexagonal center.
snowing: A billowing cloud with four six-spoked snowflakes falling beneath it.
snowman: A snowman tilted to one side, with a top hat, two dot eyes, a carrot nose, a mouth, twig arms, and three button dots on its body.

tombstone: A round-topped gravestone slab standing above a separate wide horizontal base bar, the standard marker of a grave.

toolbox: A toolbox seen from the front, with sloped shoulders, a horizontal carry handle on the left side and an oval hand-hole on the right.
tooth: A molar tooth tilted diagonally, its bumpy crown above two tapering roots.
toothbrush: A toothbrush head seen from the side with a swirl of toothpaste on its bristles, accompanied by four-pointed sparkles indicating cleanliness.
top-hat: A tall cylindrical top hat with a wide oval brim and a band around its base, associated with stage magicians and formal Victorian dress.
top-paw: A clawed beast's paw seen from above, its four splayed toes ending in long curved talons.
topaz: A teardrop-shaped gem with a pointed top, ringed by a concentric outline and a curved inner highlight.
torc: A thick neck ring with a gap at the bottom, its two tapered ends capped by large round knobs, the band notched with short grooves.
torch: A tapered torch held at a diagonal, its wide head crowned with licking flames.
tornado: A funnel-shaped whirlwind of spiraling bands, wide at the top and tapering to a narrow tail, with debris swirling around it.
tornado-discs: A descending series of tilted elliptical rings shrinking in size along a diagonal, forming a funnel-shaped whirlwind.
torpedo: A side view of a torpedo with rounded nose, banded body and tail fin, trailed by three rising bubbles.
tortoise: A tortoise in side profile with a segmented domed shell, outstretched head and neck, and stubby legs.
totem: A carved totem pole with an owl-like horned face at the top, outstretched feathered wings, stacked geometric body segments, and a flat base bar.
totem-head: A carved totem or tiki mask face with slanted almond eyes, a narrow split nose, and a wide rectangular grid of blocky bared teeth.
totem-mask: A tribal mask face with a curved brow band, angled wing-like eyebrows, hollow scowling eyes and a wide mouth of jagged pointed teeth.
toucan: A toucan's head and neck in profile, with a large elongated beak and a round eye.
tow-truck: A tow truck in side view, its cab and flatbed riding on two large wheels with a rear-mounted boom arm holding a dangling hook.
towel: A towel hanging from a wall-mounted rack, its cloth marked with two wavy stripes across the middle.
tower-bridge: Two tall spired towers pierced with rows of windows, joined by a high walkway and a lower arched roadway with suspension cables, in the manner of London's Tower Bridge.
tower-fall: A crenellated stone tower cracking apart, with a jagged fissure down its side and chunks of masonry flying off to the right.
tower-flag: A crenellated tower top with a banner on a tall pole rising above the battlements, a mark of a claimed or held stronghold.
toy-mallet: A small mallet with a diamond-shaped head and a beaded handle, with impact streaks radiating from the head.
tracked-robot: A front-facing robot with a small crested head, broad torso bearing a horizontal slot, segmented shoulder plates, and stacked tread bars forming its lower body.
trade: Two squares each bearing a diagonal arrow, linked by a pair of curved arrows sweeping in opposite directions, the standard sign for exchange or swapping.
traffic-cone: A traffic cone with banded segments rising from a wide flat base, the standard marker for hazards and roadwork.
traffic-lights-green: A traffic signal box with three round lamps stacked vertically, the bottom one filled dark, flanked by curved hoods or side flares.
traffic-lights-orange: A traffic signal box with three round lamps stacked vertically, the middle one filled dark, flanked by curved visor shapes on either side.
traffic-lights-ready-to-go: A traffic signal box on a short base with three lamps under visors, the middle one blank white and the outer two filled with dark discs.
traffic-lights-red: A traffic light housing with three stacked round lamps, the topmost one lit as a dark disc ringed by a halo, with curved visor shapes flanking each side.
trail: A winding path snaking into the distance beside a signpost with a single arrow-shaped board pointing left.
trample: A large-headed mallet or war hammer with a broad rectangular head notched at its corners atop a straight vertical handle.
transform: A filled circle joined by a thick diagonal arrow pointing down-right into a solid square, the standard sign for one thing changing into another.
transfuse: Two overlapping hearts, each half-filled with liquid, with a single drop falling from the lower point of one.
transparent-slime: An irregular splattered blob of ooze with a trailing tendril, curved highlight streaks, and a small separate droplet beside it.
transparent-tubes: Two test tubes crossed in an X, each with a rounded bottom and an elliptical rim showing a liquid surface inside.
transportation-rings: A standing human figure seen from the front, encircled by two large horizontal rings at chest and hip height, a common depiction of a teleportation platform.
trap-mask: A menacing mask with angular slanted eye slits and a wide grin of jagged interlocking fangs, tapering to a pointed chin.
trash-can: A tapered trash can marked with three vertical slots, its flat lid with a handle held above the body, the standard sign for deleting or discarding.
travel-dress: A short-sleeved dress with a V-neck bodice and a flared pleated skirt.
tread: A side view of a boot with two short lace strokes across the instep, worn on a bent leg with a flared cuff above, poised in a stomping step.
treasure-map: A ragged-edged parchment map showing mountain peaks, a dotted trail winding across it, and an X marking a spot.
trebuchet: A trebuchet siege engine: a triangular timber frame on a base supporting a pivoting throwing arm with a hanging sling pouch on one end and a heavy counterweight on the other.
tree-beehive: A domed skep beehive built of stacked bands with an arched entrance hole, surrounded by small dashes suggesting swarming bees.
tree-branch: A forking twig bearing three broad lobed leaves, one on each shoot and one at the tip.
tree-door: A broad-canopied tree whose trunk holds an arched doorway with a small round knob, suggesting a fairy or elven dwelling.
tree-face: A close-up tree trunk whose swirling bark ridges and knotholes form eye-like hollows above a large oval mouth, suggesting a face in the wood as with ents or dryads.
tree-growth: A conifer tree with tiered branches beside a large upward-pointing arrow, the standard sign for growth or increase.
tree-roots: The base of a thick tree trunk splaying into several tapering roots that spread and dig downward.
tree-swing: A thick tree trunk with a branch extending from it, from which two ropes hang down to a flat plank seat.
treehouse: A small gabled house with two square windows nestled among the billowing foliage of a broad-trunked tree.
trefoil-lily: A symmetrical three-lobed fleur-de-lis ornament with a crescent-topped central petal, curling side scrolls and a pointed downward tip, a heraldic lily emblem.
trefoil-shuriken: A circular throwing star with three curved blades sweeping around a central ring, framed by an outer band of three crescent arcs.
trench-assault: A cross-section of ground with a V-shaped trench cut into it, above a horizontal bar, with a curved arrow arcing out of the trench and over the far edge.
trench-body-armor: A sleeveless torso cuirass with riveted shoulder straps, two horizontal segmented waist plates, and a rounded groin flap below.
trench-knife: A dagger with a long tapering blade set into a knuckle-duster grip pierced by four finger holes.
trench-spade: A shovel with a straight handle and a broad pointed blade, angled diagonally across the frame.
triangle-target: A triangle formed from three tapered bars separated by gaps at each corner, in the manner of a targeting reticle.
tribal-gear: A tribal mask with round eyes and zigzag markings beside a leaf-shaped shield with stripe patterns and a slanted spear.
tribal-mask: A tribal mask face with two round eyes, a broad vertical nose stripe, and a wide zigzag row of pointed teeth above a curved chin.
tribal-pendant: A necklace cord strung with small beads holding a large oval pendant set with a faceted gem and flanked by curved feather- or wing-like blades.
tribal-shield: A teardrop-shaped tribal shield bearing a mask-like face pattern of spirals, dots and a central stem, crossed behind by two spears.
tribunal-jury: A group of faceless figures standing in two rows behind a paneled bench bearing a balance scale, the emblem of justice and the law.
triceratops-head: A triceratops head in profile, showing its spiked neck frill, nose horn and two long curved brow horns.
trident: A trident angled diagonally, its long shaft splitting into three barbed prongs with sharp arrowhead points, a weapon associated with sea gods.
trident-shield: A shield with three spiked peaks along its top edge, bearing a trident-like arrow figure with prongs pointing up and outward and a shaft ending in a downward arrowhead.
triforce: Three solid equilateral triangles arranged to form a larger triangle with a blank inverted triangle at the center, the Triforce emblem.
trigger-hurt: A solid circle hovering above a bar topped with three jagged spikes, suggesting a ball about to fall onto a trap of blades.
trilobite: A trilobite seen from above, with a domed head shield, segmented tapering body, and two long curving antennae sweeping back around it.
trinacria: A triskelion of three bent legs radiating from a round head marked with a bar and an oval, the emblem of Sicily and the Isle of Man.
triorb: Three overlapping discs arranged in a triangle, with a downward-pointing triangle outline cut through them leaving smaller triangular and lens-shaped gaps.
triple-beak: A roughly circular mass with three hooked beak-like jaws and three oval eye shapes arranged in rotational symmetry around its center.
triple-claws: Three curved, tapering claw shapes of increasing size arranged in an overlapping diagonal row, the standard mark of a beast's raking slash.
triple-corn: A circular emblem formed of three interlocking spiral-tipped horn shapes with small oval accents between them, a triskelion-like knotwork disc.
triple-gate: A gatehouse facade with a steep triangular roof marked by three stacked horizontal bars, standing on three rounded arched openings.
triple-lock: A circular emblem of three interlocking keyhole-like curved arms with round holes spiraling around a central disc, forming a triskelion-style seal.
triple-needle: Three syringes with plunger caps and long sharp needles, angled and pointing outward in different directions.
triple-plier: Three ringed discs joined in a pinwheel arrangement with curved crescent blades sweeping outward, forming a rotating triskelion-like emblem.
triple-scratches: Three parallel curved tapering gashes running diagonally, the standard mark of claw scratches.
triple-shells: Three rounded shell-like discs, each split by a narrow slit, arranged in a rotating triangular formation with curved arcs linking them.
triple-skulls: Three human skulls with gritted teeth, one large and upright above two smaller ones tilted at angles, a common emblem of death.
triple-yin: Three interlocking comma-shaped lobes swirling around a central disc, each bearing a ringed dot, forming a triple yin-yang taijitu associated with balance and cosmic harmony.
tripwire: A shoe-clad foot and leg striding forward with a taut wire stretched across its path, catching against the ankle.
triquetra: A triquetra formed of three overlapping pointed-oval arcs meeting at a central point, a Celtic knot motif associated with trinities and pagan or druidic magic.
trireme: An ancient oared galley with two billowing square sails, a row of angled oars beneath the hull, and a large eye painted near its curved prow.
triton-head: A frontal fish-man head with a domed cranium, wide flaring fin-like ears or gills, and two large round bulging eyes.
troglodyte: A hunched reptilian humanoid with a spiny crest along its back and head, clawed hands and feet, crouching forward as if about to lunge.
trojan-horse: An angular wooden horse standing on a wheeled platform, its body marked with plank lines and a hatch, the Trojan horse of Greek legend and a byword for hidden infiltration.
troll: A frontal troll head with large pointed ears, jagged fringe of hair, small narrow eyes and a broad flat snout, set against a blocky shouldered silhouette.
trombone: A trombone seen diagonally, with its flaring bell, looped tubing and extended U-shaped slide.
tron-arrow: A zigzagging arrow folding back on itself twice before ending in a large triangular head pointing to the lower right.
trophies-shelf: Three trophy cups of increasing size standing on a shelf supported by two legs, a conventional mark of victory and achievement.
trophy: A two-handled cup on a flared pedestal base with a wide rimmed bowl, the standard prize awarded for victory.
trophy-cup: A two-handled trophy cup on a stem and rectangular base plaque, the conventional award for victory or championship.
tropical-fish: A round-bodied angelfish with tall sweeping dorsal and ventral fins, a forked tail, a large round eye and a small pointed snout.
trousers: A pair of wide-legged trousers seen from the front, with a curved waistband and a narrow slit dividing the two legs.
trowel: A pointed triangular masonry trowel with a cranked shank and cylindrical handle, angled diagonally across the frame.
truce: A fist gripping a pole from which a large waving flag streams, the conventional sign of surrender or a truce when the flag is white.
truck: A side view of a cargo truck with a scalloped-hemmed canvas-covered trailer bed, a cab with a window, and three wheels.
trumpet: A trumpet angled diagonally with its flared bell, looping tubing and valve slides, and a small mouthpiece at the lower end.
trumpet-flag: A long straight trumpet with a flaring bell, hung with a swallow-tailed banner bearing a snarling wolf's head, as used by heralds announcing a lord's arrival.
trunk-mushroom: A shelf fungus with a spotted cap and gilled underside jutting sideways from the trunk of a tree.
tuba: A tuba with a wide upward-flaring bell, looping tubing, three valve buttons, and a mouthpipe extending to one side.
tumbleweed: A tangled ball of dry twisting branches coiled into a spiral knot with loose spiky ends jutting out, as in desert scrub blown by wind.
tumor: A rounded mass built from clustered irregular blobs and lobes with small oval voids, suggesting a cluster of cells or a lumpy growth.
tumulus: A rounded earthen mound sprouting spiky grass tufts, with a stone-lined passage entrance cut into its side and small boulders at its base, depicting an ancient burial barrow.
tune-pitch: A single eighth note with a flowing double flag, its stem crossing horizontal staff lines that run to the left and right edges.
tunisia: The silhouetted map outline of Tunisia, a tall irregular landmass tapering to a point at its southern tip.
turban: A turban formed of broad wrapped cloth bands crossing in front, topped with a plume feather rising from the center.
turbine: A jet engine seen at a three-quarter angle, its bladed fan disc with central hub set at the mouth of a tapering nacelle housing.
turd: A coiled pile of dung with a swirled tip, flanked by wavy stink lines and small floating specks above it.
turnstile: A turnstile post with a slot panel and three radiating horizontal arms fanning out from its rotating hub, the kind of gate found at entrances and ticket barriers.
turret: A tank-style gun turret seen from the side, with a boxy housing and long barrel extending right, mounted above a small block on a wide flared base.
turtle: A sea turtle seen from above, with an oval shell marked by hexagonal plate patterning, four paddle-like flippers, a rounded head and a short pointed tail.
turtle-shell: An oval turtle shell with a notch at the top, its surface divided into a central hexagonal plate ringed by angular scutes.
tusks-flag: A hanging banner marked with a pale upraised hand, flanked by two curving tusks and topped by crossed sweeping tusk shapes.
tv: A boxy vintage television set with a rounded screen, a round knob and three slot-like controls on its side panel, and a V-shaped rabbit-ear antenna on top.
tv-remote: A tilted handheld remote control bearing a round directional pad with a cross cut through it, rows of circular buttons, and several small rectangular keys.
tv-tower: The upper section of a broadcast tower, with a bulbous spherical observation pod split by a band, a tapering shaft below and an antenna mast with small vertical struts above.
twin-shell: A round disc cut by two interlocking spiral arms curling into a central whorl, resembling a shell coil or a hurricane swirl.
twirl-center: A disc of curved blades spiraling inward around a small solid dot at the center, like a vortex or camera-shutter swirl.
twirly-flower: A flower with five broad curved petals swirling pinwheel-fashion around a solid round center.
twister: A tornado funnel drawn as stacked swirling bands tapering downward, touching down beside jagged blades of grass or debris.
two-coins: Two thick round coins lying at angles and overlapping, seen in perspective as flat discs with visible edges.
two-feathers: Two overlapping plumed feathers with pointed tips, ragged notched lower edges and slender curving quills trailing to the lower right.
two-handed-sword: A long straight-bladed sword angled diagonally, with a curved crossguard, long grip, and rounded pommel.
two-shadows: Three featureless standing human figures, the central one solid black and the two flanking it drawn as empty outlines, suggesting duplicates or shadow copies.
tyre: A thick ring tilted in perspective into an ellipse, seen at an angle so its inner rim and side wall both show, like a tyre lying askew.
ubisoft-sun: A sun whose disc is drawn as a coiled spiral, ringed by twelve short tapering rays.
udder: A cow's udder, a rounded dome-shaped bag hanging with four tapering teats pointing downward and outward.
ufo: A flying saucer with a domed canopy and round porthole lights, projecting a widening beam of light downward.
ultrasound: A dot emitting expanding concentric sound waves that strike a wine glass, cracking it with a jagged split down its bowl.
uluru: A broad low mesa with fissured slopes rising above a flat horizontal ground bar, with a round sun or moon disc in the sky above.
umbrella: An umbrella with a domed canopy of separated panels above a straight shaft ending in a hooked handle, a common emblem of protection or shelter.
umbrella-bayonet: A furled umbrella with a hooked crook handle, its tip extending into a long pointed blade.
unbalanced: A tilted plank resting on a triangular fulcrum, with a square block weighing down its low end and a circle above the raised end.
uncertainty: A question mark with a separate dot below, encircled by a thick arc ending in two downward-pointing arrowheads.
underground-cave: A cavern cross-section with stalactites hanging from the ceiling above an uneven rocky floor rising into mounds.
underhand: A curved arrow sweeping down into a low scoop and rising steeply to a triangular point, tracing an underhand throwing motion.
underwear: A pair of briefs seen from the front, with a broad elastic waistband above the narrowing crotch panel and leg openings.
underwear-shorts: A pair of boxer briefs seen from the front, with a separate horizontal waistband bar above the flared legs.
unfriendly-fire: A curling flame with jagged spikes, bearing a fanged snarling mouth and a slit eye, forming a menacing living fire creature.
unicorn: A unicorn's head and neck in profile, with a long spiraling horn, pointed ear and streaming mane.
unicycle: A unicycle: a single wheel with a hub, two opposed pedals, and a vertical seat post topped by a saddle.
union-jack: Four corner clusters of straight and diagonal bars converging toward the center, forming the overlapping crosses of the British Union Jack flag.
unlit-bomb: A round cannonball bomb with a short angled fuse holder and a long S-curved wick trailing from it.
unlit-candelabra: A three-branched candelabrum on a domed base, holding straight candles with bare wicks and no flames.
unlocking: A key with an oval bow and toothed shaft pointing toward a keyhole shape, the standard sign for unlocking access.
unplugged: A rounded electrical plug with two prongs and a trailing cord, drawn separated from a socket block with two matching slots.
unstable-orb: A sphere containing a jagged zigzag bolt and shard shapes, ringed by crooked lightning-like spikes radiating outward.
unstable-projectile: A circular projectile marked with jagged lightning-like cracks, trailing sweeping streaks and small dots behind it as it hurtles forward.
up-card: A broad trapezoidal base from which a large upward-pointing arrow rises, its shaft cut out of the block below.
upgrade: Four stacked upward-pointing chevrons decreasing in size toward the bottom, a common sign for advancement or leveling up.
uprising: A crowd of faceless figures with raised fists holding aloft a pitchfork, a burning torch and a sickle, the standard image of a peasant revolt or mob.
ursa-major: A constellation diagram of seven spiked stars joined by straight lines into a dipper-shaped figure with a bowl and a curving handle, the Big Dipper of Ursa Major.
uruguay: A solid silhouette of the country of Uruguay's territory, with straight upper edges and a rounded, bulging lower-right coastline.
usa-flag: The Stars and Stripes flag of the United States, with a canton of five-pointed stars beside horizontal bars.
usable: An open hand with fingers and thumb spread, set within a thick ring.
usb-key: A USB flash drive angled diagonally, its beveled body separated by a thin gap from the metal connector tip marked with two small square holes.
ushanka: A fur cap with raised side flaps and a lowered front flap, bearing a five-pointed star on its crown, the classic Russian winter hat.
uzi: A compact Uzi-style submachine gun seen from the side, with boxy receiver, short barrel stub, trigger guard and a magazine extending from the grip.
vacuum-cleaner: A canister vacuum cleaner with a wheeled body, a looping curved hose, and a wand ending in a wide floor nozzle.
valley: A jagged mountain range rising above a flat plain that is split by a narrow zigzag crevasse or gorge.
valve: A pipeline valve seen head-on, with a horizontal handle bar atop a stem and a central body bearing a water droplet, flanked by pipe sections.
vampire-cape: A standing figure with a blank oval head wearing a high-collared cloak that flares into pointed tails, the classic silhouette of a vampire.
vampire-dracula: A vampire's head with a widow's-peak hairline, pointed ears, angular brows and fanged mouth, rising from a high-collared cape.
van-damme-split: A headband-wearing figure with arms crossed, performing a horizontal side split with each leg resting on top of a separate upright pillar.
vanilla-flower: A blossom with several narrow, curving, pointed petals radiating pinwheel-fashion from a small open center.
velocipede: A penny-farthing bicycle with a large front wheel bearing pedal cranks, a small rear wheel, curved frame, saddle and handlebar.
velociraptor: A raptor dinosaur silhouette in profile, standing on clawed hind legs with a long tapering tail, small grasping forelimbs and a toothy jaw.
velociraptor-tracks: A pair of two-toed dinosaur footprints, each with separate pointed claw marks ahead of the toes.
vending-machine: A vending machine cabinet with a glass front showing shelves of stocked items, a side control panel with keypad and coin slot, and a dispensing tray below.
venezuela: An elephant in profile facing left, its trunk curled upward and a large ear and tusk visible.
venus-flytrap: A Venus flytrap head with two spiked, toothed lobes, flanked by a curved tapering leaf at its base.
venus-of-willendorf: A squat, corpulent female figurine with heavy breasts, wide hips and a braided cap over a faceless head, the prehistoric Venus fertility idol.
vertical-banner: A hanging pennant banner with a pointed lower edge and a matching chevron stripe, suspended from a horizontal rod with arrow-shaped finials and a small tab above.
vertical-flip: A straight double-headed arrow pointing up and down, the common sign for vertical movement, resizing, or flipping.
vhs: A VHS videocassette seen face-on, with a window revealing the two spools and the tape stretched between them.
vial: A round-bottomed test tube with a flared rim, half-filled with bubbling liquid, with two bubbles escaping above the mouth.
vibrating-ball: A solid black sphere surrounded by two broken concentric arcs offset diagonally, the usual shorthand for vibration or radiating waves.
vibrating-shield: A heater-style shield with a thick border and solid inner field, surrounded by three detached arc segments echoing its outline to suggest shaking or a pulsing barrier.
vibrating-smartphone: A smartphone with a blank screen, speaker slot and round button, flanked by curved arcs radiating outward on both sides to indicate shaking or buzzing.
video-camera: A shoulder-mounted camcorder in side view, with a lens hood, top handle, microphone barrel, and hinged viewfinder arm.
video-conference: A monitor on a stand showing a head-and-shoulders bust, with a small ring-shaped camera lens above the screen.
viking-church: A tiered Norse stave church seen from the front, its stacked steep gabled roofs topped by dragon-head finials and a small spire above a central doorway.
viking-head: A bearded warrior's head in profile wearing a horned helmet, with long flowing hair and beard, the conventional image of a Viking.
viking-helmet: A horned helmet with a domed cap, a central segmented nose guard ending in a point, and a riveted brow band with two oval eye slits.
viking-longhouse: A Norse longhouse seen from the front, with a steep thatched roof flanked by curved crossed gable beams, sitting above a broad plinth and a row of vertical posts.
viking-shield: A round shield with vertical plank bands, a central boss ringed by circles, and horizontal arrow-like reinforcements crossing it.
vile-fluid: A teardrop-shaped droplet bearing an angry face with slanted eyes and a wide fanged grin, a common mark for poison or corrupted liquid.
village: A cluster of simple houses with steep triangular roofs, square windows and doorways, overlapping at different sizes to suggest a settlement.
vine-flower: A five-petaled blossom with a radiating spiked center, surrounded by curling tendrils and spirals suggesting vines.
vine-leaf: A three-lobed vine leaf with veins cut into its blades, topped by a curling tendril that loops back on itself.
vine-whip: A long curling vine or thorny tendril looping diagonally, with hooked barbs and small leaf-like spurs branching off along its length.
vines: Curving vine stems crossing the frame, some bearing small pointed leaves and others trailing coiled tendrils.
vintage-robot: A boxy robot with a domed head, a large circle on its square torso, curved arms ending in pincer claws, and two stubby legs.
viola: A pansy blossom seen face-on, with three broad rounded petals spreading around a circular center divided by curving lines.
violin: A violin seen at a diagonal with its scrolled neck and tuning pegs, a bow laid across the body's strings.
virgo: The Virgo zodiac glyph, an M-like figure whose final stroke curls back across itself in a loop, denoting the astrological sign of the Virgin.
virtual-marker: A large diamond split into upper and lower chevrons with a small solid diamond at its center, crossed by a horizontal bar.
virus: A bacteriophage with a hexagonal head, banded tail sheath, and splayed angular tail fibers at its base.
visored-helm: A knight's helmet seen from the front, with a domed skull, a slotted visor of vertical breathing bars, and a flared chin and gorget.
vitruvian-man: A figure with outstretched arms and legs framed by a circle and a square, after Leonardo's Vitruvian Man and a byword for human proportion.
volcano: An erupting volcanic cone with curved streamers of lava and debris arcing upward and outward from its summit crater.
volleyball-ball: A volleyball, its sphere divided by curving seam lines into sweeping panels.
vomiting: A round face with squeezed-shut eyes and a wide gaping mouth from which a thick stream spews downward.
voodoo-doll: A stitched rag figure with tufted hair, round eyes and a jagged toothy grin, pierced through the body by two long pins.
vortex: A spiral whirlpool of curved tapering blades sweeping inward to a small hooked eye at the center.
vote: A hand dropping a folded paper ballot into the slot of a boxy ballot box whose front panel bears a jagged mountain-like design.
vr-headset: A head wearing a wide visor-style VR headset with a small round indicator light, a strap over the crown, and a cable curving down at the side.
vulture: A hunched perching bird in profile with a hooked beak, round pale eye and long swept tail feathers, standing on a mound.
vuvuzelas: Three flared horn trumpets with wide bell mouths and tapering tubes, fanned out and pointing in different directions.
walk: A person in profile mid-stride, arms and legs swinging in opposite directions, the standard pedestrian walking figure.
walkie-talkie: A pair of handheld two-way radios, each with an upright antenna, speaker grille bars, a round knob and a short signal stroke beside it.
walking-boot: A high-topped boot seen from the side with a folded cuff and thick sole, tilted as if mid-stride.
walking-scout: A hunched figure in a wide-brimmed hat and cape striding forward on angular legs, with motion streaks trailing behind.
walking-turret: A blocky mechanical walker with a bulky body, a long protruding gun barrel and a small round lens, standing on four jointed spindly legs.
wall-light: A wall-mounted lantern with a pointed cap and flared tapering body, held out from a wall plate by a curved scrolling bracket arm.
wallet: A billfold wallet with a round button clasp on its flap, several cards or banknotes fanning out from the top.
walrus-head: A front-facing walrus head with round eyes, a whiskered muzzle split into two dotted cheek pads, and tusks hanging below.
walther-ppk: A semi-automatic pistol seen in profile, with slide, hammer, trigger inside its guard, and textured grip.
wanted-reward: A tattered wanted poster nailed up by a tack, reading "WANTED" above a framed portrait of a hatted figure and two blank text bars.
war-axe: A single-bladed war axe with a broad crescent blade bearing an eye-like motif, its long haft ending in a spike and studded with barbs.
war-bonnet: A Native American feathered war bonnet, its long plumes fanning out from a beaded headband with trailing feathers hanging below.
war-pick: A war pick with two long curved spikes sweeping from an ornamented head, mounted on a wrapped diagonal haft.
warehouse: A tall storage shelving unit with a vertical ladder at its right side, its shelves loaded with boxes, crates, bars and round objects.
warhammer: A war hammer with a long diagonal haft, a blocky wrapped head with a curved spike on one side and small shards flying off the other.
warlock-eye: A pointed, angular eye with a pale round iris marked by a downward dagger-shaped pupil, ringed by radiating shards of light.
warlock-hood: A pointed hood or cowl with a banded brow and long side flaps, framing an empty dark void where a face would be.
warlord-helmet: A horned helmet with a pointed faceplate, narrow angular eye slits and flaring cheek guards, an emblem of barbarian warlords.
warp-pipe: A stout vertical pipe with a wide flared collar ring at its top opening, in the manner of a Mario-style warp pipe.
